To sum it up...

It's comfortable structurally, and materials wise. It rocks just so, and it assembles quick.

1. Buy or Do Not Buy?,Buy It.,2. What is so good about this?,It is a unique toy, so much fun. It’s a mini helicopter/drone, but packs quite a punch. It is affordable, and so worth the entertainment you receive in return. The basic idea is it floats up in the air like a helicopter, and comes down. Your job is to position an object or your hand under the toy as it drops to trigger it to fly straight back up again, the longer your hand/object is placed under the toy, the higher the toy will rise. The toy lights up beautifully, which makes playing in the dark super fun, inside or outside.,3. How do you play with it?,Don’t make the mistake I made, and not read the instructions. Actually, I still haven’t read it 😊, and figure out how to play with it correctly by purely by accident, albeit after several knocks and falls…of the toy, not me. Turn on the toy by pressing the black rubber button at the bottom of the toy. Hold the toy on your hand upright, press the button on the remote to turn on the blades, then let it go. No need to push it up…just let it go. As it floats up and comes down, just place your hand under the toy to make it rise again.,To avoid potentially damaging the toy, know that there is a sensor under the body (ball) of the toy. The longer your hand or any object is under the sensor, the higher the toy will rise. So, when you get started playing with the toy, and wonder like I did, why it keeps going up and being stuck on the ceiling, you are probably placing your hand under the sensor for too long. No worries, if you are too short to grab the toy as it floats under the ceiling, just press the button again, and after a couple of seconds, you will notice the blades slow down and the toy drop, just press the button again to make it rise again to avoid hitting the floor.,4. How much of playtime do you get with it?,About 10 minutes. I charge it for about 20 minutes, and have been getting about 10 minutes of continuous play time. Given the size of the toy, I think this is probably as long as the charge can hold.,5. Is it safe?,I think so. The blades are plastic, and flexible. They are not hard. As long as you play it the right away, you should not hurt yourself. Also, the fact that it floats up means that it will rise anytime something is under it, so the chances of it hitting your eyes or injuring you otherwise is small as long as you are not throwing it horizontally. The ball/base is clear plastic. It is not heavy or metal-like, so no danger there. Small kids should play under adult supervision.

review_title: Not like the microscopes I remember as a kid
review_text: ,  Your browser does not support HTML5 video.,        ,   Wow, microscopes have come a long way. Our son was using something similar is school recently and expressed a desire to have one at home. This is pretty awesome. You can view everything on the large, bright screen, and even take photos and video. It has a built-in light so everything is ready to view. He has a great time using this on the various things he finds in the yard, such as leaves, bugs (yuck), and even flowers.

I finally broke down and bought a microscope after inadvertently wiping the serial number off a microchip while scrubbing at conformal covering over a PCB - that serial is just painted on and my 99.9% isopropyl wiped it right out like BAM! The polymer coating didn't even slow it down. All my other magnifiers are less-than perfect in best cases, and just plain useless here. I knew there had to be microns of paint left but I needed more magnification. I still didn't expect to get better than a vague idea of what the printed characters might have been with any grade microscope.,This thing exceeded my expectations in the first 10 seconds of use. Unlike another microscope I have (a little handheld deal), this magnifies clear down to 10x - typically when it says "micro" on it the thing wants to start at 60x or 100x. I read it in the product promo material and honestly didn't believe it'd go that low - figured it had to be a mistake. Between a legitimate 10x magnification, an absolutely phenomenal LED lighting package (that floods the item directly under the lens with white light), and an adjustable material-bench, I was able to get a crystal clear image of the otherwise scattered flecks of paint left on the IC in question. I believe the built-in lighting package helped immensely - I seriously get an enhanced image that's as clear as it would have been when the paint was fresh. The LCD display quality is unbelievable too.

As the kids stay home more often now with our current situation, I decided to buy this digital microscope to help them have fun with experimenting with microscopes.  I would search on the web for microscope experiments for kids and do those with them.  It's very educational and fun.  This microscope really impressed me.  The picture quality is really clear.  The built in light is adjustable.  It comes with a 8GB SD card so you can save pictures and the microscope even has an option to record videos.  For taking pictures, just press the OK button.  Hold down the OK button to switch it over to recording mode.  The left and right arrow zooms in and out but holding on the left arrow will flip or invert the screen.  That's a really cool feature.  I like that it comes with 2 sample slides to get you started (honeybee wings and onion epidermis).  I like the fact that it uses the 18650 lithium rechargeable which lasts pretty long and I have a lot of those batteries.  It was easy for me to connect the microscope to my windows 10 desktop.  I didn't have to download any drivers or applications.  For this, I just needed to connect the micro USB cable to the computer and choose mass storage on the microscope.  I did have to format the 8GB micro SD card before I was able to take pictures and record videos.  Instead of the mass storage you can choose the PC camera.  This option will allow you to display the microscope image on your computer.  There is so much you can do with this, it's just amazing.  Overall, I am very pleased with this purchase.

review_title: Excellent tool for close electronics work.  Great for kids too.
review_text: Unlike old-style optical microscopes, where you have to adjust either a single or double eyepiece to your vision and then play with focusing, this unit projects the image onto a screen a little larger than a cell phone. All you have to do is set the amount of magnification and adjust the focus. And you do that while looking at the screen so it's very easy. I use it for soldering onto PCB boards, and it makes the job effortless. I would also think that kids in biology class would benefit from having something like this, as it's much easier to operate than an old optical microscope. The unit seems fairly solid and in fact dropped off the table at one point without damage. The image is clear sharp and full of contrast. It's just a very impressive unit for the price.

With this feature, you can place the multi-meter pointing to the wire/outlet without any wire connecting to the multi-meter, it will show you if the wire is live and if it's producing high or low voltage.  It uses standard AA battery vs most which uses the 9V battery.  I like how this is designed where even with the case wrapping around the multi-meter, you can easily change the battery without taking the case off.  With my old one, I have to remove the case which is very annoying to change the battery.  Overall, I am very satisfy with this digital multi-meter.

review_text: When I received it, I was frankly expecting to spend fruitless hours downloading the app, fiddling with batteries and trying to get the station itself connected to the included outdoor sensor and/or to wifi. After putting batteries in the unit and the sensor (5 AA batteries, 3 and 2 respectively), I opted to download the app and continue the initial startup process through my iPad.,There are 6 kinds of the weather forecast, calendar, clock, automatic snooze function, backlight, alarm clock function, the moon phase display, indoor and outdoor air pressure + temperature, min./max. Display for humidity + temperature, the trend of humidity and temperature, outdoor thermometer and frost alarm, date in 7 different languages: English, German, Italian, French, Spanish, Dutch and Danish.,You can also set the monitor up manually, but I wanted to have the monitor to connect to the National Weather Service for forecasts. All it really took was enabling the camera on my mobile device and scanning the bar code on the rear of the unit for the app to begin the process. The bottom line is everything fell into place and I had the new sensor placed outdoors and the monitor hanging on the wall within 10 minutes start to finish. Word of caution here for those with dual band routers. Like many "Internet of Things" wireless articles, the monitor will only connect to a 2.4 GHz network and the mobile device on which the app is running MUST BE CONNECTED TO YOUR 2.4 GHz NETWORK. If your mobile device is connected to your 5 GHz network, you will frustrate the heck out of yourself trying to get the monitor connected to wifi, as it will fail every time. Once you are through the setup process, you can switch back to your home 5 GHz network. This is noted in the Quick Start guide but it is easy to miss. The sharp color screen of the digital weather station will illuminate continuously with a USB charging cable during power operation, and when charging by USB, there are 4 different models of brightness. To save energy from batteries, the LCD color display would not light up automatically in battery mode. You can touch the top of the weather station, then it will become evoked.,The ability to remotely view weather conditions at one's home and the NWS forecast are nice features. Certainly not for the true meteorology aficionado but more than enough for a quick and dirty view of the weather.

review_title: Best purchase I’ve made in 2020 so far.
review_text: Boy oh boy this has been a game changer. I’ve made some excellent cooked meats with this device. Cooking by temperature is the best way...who would’ve knew! It can also be manually customized to whatever settings you choose. The probes are impressively durable made with Teflon and confidently survived my super hot Weber grill. It came with 4 probes making it possible to cook different foods and measure both air and meat internal temperature simultaneously! The probes connect with outside device, allowing me to get better cooks because I don’t have to open the grill to check on my food and release heat.  I get a notification on my phone when the food is ready. The range is long and reliable, giving me peace of mine to tend to my guests and not worry about the grill. The set up is fairly easy and straight forward- I just scanned the barcode in the manual with my phone app. So happy with this product. Recommending to friends and family for sure!

The other thermometer that I used was/is a very expensive "quick-read" thermometer that I have used and trusted over the years. So, I would say that this gives a very accurate reading. I like the probes and the Bluetooth function/app ~ it makes it very convenient.,The second time using this, was today (Easter Sunday). I used it to monitor the temperature of a ham that we were cooking in the oven. Again, it was very convenient and made it easy to know when the ham got to the desired temperature, without having to constantly open the oven and check. Again, after I removed the ham, I double-checked the temperature with my other meat thermometer and the reading was nearly identical (within a couple degrees). 👍,My next "test" will be when I go camping (hopefully) in the next couple of weeks. I really like that it is portable and comes with a convenient carry case. I have been looking at similar meat thermometers over the years and they were just too expensive. I was somewhat skeptical going into this purchase (based on the price), but so far - I am pleased and... I am impressed 😁,I would recommend this for anyone that is considering. It is easy to use and takes a lot of guesswork out of your cooking, giving me peace of mind that my meat is being safely cooked. Good purchase 👍

If for some reason the G20 starts out a little bit too boomy, readjust the equalizer to reduce the low/mid frequencies a bit. Be sure to fit the correct sized tips for your ears. As for bluetooth performance, the AirPods and Galaxy Buds default to the AAC codec while the other three streams bluetooth through SBC. Based on my experience so far, the Apt-X codec streaming quality is amazing on the S9+.,On a side note, I've read  a lot of reviews and noticed that some users have had issues with the volume suddenly decrease on one side. review_text: My husband mentioned wanting one of these some time ago after seeing my brother use one to retrieve a screw he dropped near his engine that was otherwise out of sight, but I kind of forgot about it to be honest. It wasn't just any old screwdriver, because it belonged to his grandfather who engraved his initial in the carved wood handle,and seriously was a really nice screwdriver.  We assumed since it was a return vent on the 1st floor, it would end up in the crawl space, but it didn't because the vents vent out to other venting within the crawlspace.  He ended up fashioning an old cell phone on a string hooking to our broom to try and record where it may have ended up, but the clip holding the string to the phone and broom ended up snapping off when he hit the side of a vent, and now both the phone and screwdriver were missing. He was feeling defeated, so gave up on the project for a bit knowing he could come back to it later.,I remembered how handy my brother's scope was, so decided to purchase this one for him with Father's Day being days away, after scouting out several of them.  This one had all of the features my brother mentioned would be good in a scope, and was in my price range.  He was really excited and being a techy guy anyway, couldn't wait to break it out.  Of course he's also a cheesy guy, so used it to look at the back of his mouth and up his nose, kind of a thing, to get a giggle out of our daughter.  Dads...,Anyway, I reminded him that he could use it in the vent, which didn't dawn on him until that moment, so he jumped to his feet and looked like a man on a mission.  He fed the hose through the vent and it turns out the vent winds down slightly before opening up to the crawl space, and the screwdriver and phone were safely tucked away in a curve of the vent.  After some tapping from the first floor on the vent to figure out where he should be looking in the crawl space, my husband was able to semi-easily open it up and retrieve his treasures.  I'm sure this thing will come in handy many times over for various projects and knowing how clumsy both of us can be with dropping things.

One of the biggest issues with bleeding hydraulics is having to pump out the air bubbles. In most cases you need to have somebody in the cab pumping the clutch or the brake until all the air is out. This brake line bleeder kit includes two hoses. One of them you would use to pull brake fluid right out of the master cylinder. And the other hoes has the connector which connects to the bleeder valve on the brake caliper. This is the hose that I used and this is how I used this kit.
1. Filled up they refilling bottle with Dot 4 brake fluid which my car requires. Pulled out the filter on the top of the master cylinder and set it aside. Turned the refill bottle upside down and inserted the end into the top of the master cylinder. Tightened up they clap with the thumb screw. This ensures that brake fluid being evacuated from the cylinders is replaced with brand new brake fluid. This ensures that no air gets into brake lines.
2. Always start with the rear tire farthest away from the master cylinder on the opposite corner. My master cylinder is right in front of the steering wheel, so I plug this into the brake caliper on the passenger side rear wheel.
3. Connected the vacuum unit to my air compressor quick connect fitting. And connected the caliper hose which also has a quick connect fitting. Then connected the other end of the drain hose to the brake caliper bleeder valve.
4. Then I opened up the valve and pressed and all on the vacuum. I watched fluid come out and waited till I got about an inch to an inch and a half of fluid on the bottom of the vacuum container. I then close the valve and removed the hose from the valve and put the tire back on.
5. I then did the driver side rear brake caliper the same method and drained about another inch of fluid.
6. I then did both front brake calipers. These have less fluid in the lines because they are closer to the engine. I got about another inch to an inch and a half combined from both of the front brake calipers. On the 4th brake caliper I could see cleaner fluid coming into the vacuum container. I closed the valve and both front wheels back on.
7. I then turned on the car and pump the brakes to build pressure. I put the car in reverse and backed up a little and braked a couple of times. my brakes work perfectly and have brand new clean brake fluid.
8. I poured the dirty brake fluid into the empty dot 4 brake fluid containers and I'll take them to my local hazardous material drop off site.

review_title: Flexible gas/propane power generation at decent cost
review_text: I am personally not a fan of gas generators, but there are many advantages they have over battery power stations. In my home, we have a Jackery Explorer 1000 and Goal Zero Yeti 500x lithium-ion battery power stations, and my dad has a Honda EU2200i (1800W – 2200W) gas generator. He asked me to get him a 10 kW one for emergencies after having lost power in his neighborhood a few times, understandably upsetting him when food could spoil and 105F degree weather would keep him from comfortably sleeping during the day (he works at night.) 10,000W is overkill, in my opinion, but he likes the flexibility to have it power anything (even an electric vehicle!),My dad and I each use our gas generator/battery power stations for different reasons. He wants comfort for his home during the power outages. I want comfort while camping/traveling. For some, generators/power stations are necessary to keep medical devices, critical medicines (that need to stay refrigerated or frozen), and/or home businesses running uninterrupted. For others who live in emergency-prone areas (ie. those affected by hurricanes, tornadoes, tsunamis, earthquakes), generators can be LIFE SAVERS!,But which power generation device should you buy? It depends on your needs. In this review, we will briefly look into the Pros and Cons between gas generators, propane generators, and battery power stations, then dive into what I like and dislike about this Enkeeo dual-fuel generator.,As I had already said, I am not a fan of gas generators. So, I started looking into solar-rechargeable, lithium-ion power stations, and the closest one I could find to 10,000W was the Goal Zero Yeti 6000x that has not yet been made available. Price tag: $5,000! No, that is just too much for my dad to spend. So, a gas generator it is.,GAS GENERATORS VS PROPANE GENERATORS,PROS for Gasoline over Propane,- Gas is more easily available since gas stations are everywhere,- More efficient,-- Higher BTU (heat) production per gallon of fuel (by about 30%), making gas cheaper to operate than propane,- Less expensive to own,- Smaller, more portable,- Most popular type of generator,- More reliable in cold climates (propane tank regulators are susceptible to freezing),- Usually have on-board fuel tanks (Propane tends to be in exterior tanks),CONS against Gasoline over Propane,- Highly flammable and riskier to store near a home,- Louder than propane generators,- Dirtier-burning than propane,- Worse for the environment and more harmful to humans and pets,- Worse for generator’s lifespan due to a higher release amount of toxins and carbon deposits in the engine,- Gas has shorter shelf life than propane (degrades after about 1 year),-- Even if not used, gas needs to be replaced every so often (every 6 months),-- Propane does not expire, but the propane tank does at around 12 years,-- In a disaster, gas stations may cease operation, and you would be out of gas,--- Gas is higher in demand during emergencies,--- Propane is stored in cylinders that can last for a long time,GAS GENERATORS VS BATTERY POWER STATIONS,PROS for Gasoline over Battery,- Can run virtually forever for as long as fuel is available,-- Battery power stations will eventually run out. They can be recharged via solar panels, but that will depend on sun availability,- Longer shelf life than batteries,-- Lithium-ion batteries have a lifespan of 500 cycles. They will continue to operate past that, but efficiency will start to degrade,- Much cheaper upfront than batteries, but maintenance cost may negate that over time,CONS against Gasoline over Battery,- Should NEVER be operated indoor or in partially-enclosed areas (even with ventilation),-- Carbon monoxide gets generated and can kill you,- Must be kept at least 3’ from any structure during use,-- Battery power stations can be used anywhere, even inside or next to a house (or car!),- Fuel is highly flammable, toxic, and bad for the environment and your health,- Loud (battery stations run nearly silent and can be used throughout the night at camp sites),-- Cannot be used past a certain time at camp sites (usually 10pm),- Constant maintenance required (ie. changing of fuel every 3-6 months),- Gasoline may not be available during emergencies,-- Gas stations tend to run out fast during those times. Batteries can be recharged via solar panels,- Not as portable as battery power stations,-- Requires more care to transport,-- More cumbersome to take on camping trips,Now, let’s look at the Enkeeo Dual-Fuel Generator.,WHO IS ENKEEO?,According to the company’s website, Enkeeo “designs and builds outdoor [equipment] that [empowers] travel enthusiasts, adventurers, athletes… and gym lovers to make personal breakthroughs and achieve higher goals in their [lives].”,Their product portfolio includes camping and hiking gear, skateboards, bicycles and accessories, gears for winter/fishing/snorkeling, electric bikes, and fitness equipment.,I had previously purchased one of their smaller, lithium-ion battery power stations.,ENKEEO GENERATOR PROS,- Option to power by gas or propane (LPG) through a simple switch,-- Flexibility to choose whichever fuel source is available during an emergency (gas stations usually run out first),-- Propane is safer to store near a home whereas gas is more efficient,--- You can choose which fuel type you want to use for the task at hand,- Priced lower than most dual-fuel generators in its class,- When used with gas: 9,000W running power with surge/peak of 12,000W. See TIPS section on what this means,-- When used with Propane: 8,100W running power with surge/peak of 10,800W,- Decently-sized 459cc V-OHV electric engine (3,570 – 3,810 RPM),-- Enough to run for about 7-8 hours on a full tank (7.9 gal) at half load,--- Ran test until about 3 gallons was used, then calculated run time from there,- Multiple GFCI 120V/240V AC and DC sockets and outputs,-- 50A, 30A, 20A, 12V DC, USB,--- NEMA 14-50R (250V rated) plug is typically found in RV parks and can be used to charge electric cooking ranges and electric vehicles,--- 12V DC can be used to power a car freezer (ie. my current favorite, the Foho 54qt BCD-52), though that’s what I use my battery power station for,-- Outlets are covered against weather damage/pollution,-- AC and DC circuit breakers built-in,- Built-in 1,600 mAh 12V lithium-ion battery (19.2 Wh),-- Can be used to top off mobile device charges via USB (battery is not big enough to fully charge multiple devices from empty to full),- Enough power to run a WHOLE HOUSE through the 50A 4-hole socket, including multiple freezers, fridges, LED lights, portable Air conditioner, and other devices,-- WARNING: You need to have the proper equipment installed by a licensed electrician before you plug the generator into your house! Doing it incorrectly could ELECTROCUTE not just you, but also your neighbors and utility workers outside!,-- An entire RV uses about 3,000W on average,- Two ways to start engine: recoil or electric,- Instruction manual was easy to follow and contained just a few, grammatical errors,-- Assembly was simple: install wheels and foot brackets, then connect the battery,- Professional, tough look with a pleasing color scheme,- Wheel makes generator portable,- Free freight shipping (through Prime) was handled through a third party arranged by Amazon,-- They called to schedule a date and time. Someone must be at home to receive the item,- Included items: 2x double plugs, 2x 4-hole plug, 3-hole plug, relief valve, extension bar, 12V DC port cable, spark plug socket, tool bag, and instruction manual,- Starter 10W-30 engine oil included,- 1 year warranty,ENKEEO GENERATOR CONS,In addition to the things I dislike about gas/propane generators in general, here are specific ones against the Enkeeo:,- Heavy and large, though smaller than most propane generators and some gas ones,- Loud (more than 100 dB, depending on conditions), though the built-in vibration dampening helps lower the noise a bit,- Built-in, lithium-ion battery is a meager 1,600 mAh (19.2 Wh),-- If it were larger (500 Wh or more) AND removable, this would have been a GREAT bonus to have. It would give the ability to power electronics throughout the night without having the engine running,-- If the company could add MC4 or Anderson connected solar panel charging (with MPPT), that would further help reduce the reliance on gas/propane, making this generator the ultimate piece of equipment for emergencies,--- Enkeeo already makes portable, battery power stations,- Not shut-off for the built-in battery,I forgot to fully test the engine’s efficiency and won’t go back to see my parents for a while due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Cheaper generators could burn up more fuel than expensive ones, requiring you to refill the tank more often. From what I remember, this Enkeeo was decent.,TIPS,USAGE,- If you do not know how to use this generator, ask someone who does,-- Incorrect usage could cause damage, injury, and/or death to the engine, you, your home and devices, and even your neighbors/utility workers outside!,- Buy fuel in smaller quantities and store in clean containers,-- Less chances of all fuel getting contaminated,-- Best fuel: unleaded gasoline with less than 10% added ethanol,--- Never use E85 fuel. Don’t mix oil with gasoline,- When engine is in use, change its oil after the first 5 hours, then every 50 hours,- Change engine oil every 3-6 months or add a fuel stabilizer,-- Gasoline deteriorates after a year and can damage your engine over time if not changed,- Change air filter once a year to maintain efficiency,RUNNING VS PEAK/SURGE WATTAGE,Generator runs at 9,000W with a surge of 12,000W when used with gas. With propane, that is 8,100W and 10,800W, respectively. What does all this mean?,Electric devices always start at a higher wattage than when they are already running. For illustration purposes, let’s PRETEND the generator only provides a running output of 300W and a peak/surge of 1,200W:,Running/Continuous Output:  As long as a device (or combination of multiple ones) does not exceed 300W, it can be used,- A TV that uses 100W can be used because it is less than 300W. You can add more devices for as long as they do not exceed 300W combined,- An 1,800W miter saw, because it exceeds 300W, cannot be used,Peak/Surge Output: Almost every device temporarily draws more power when it is turned on. The highest amount it pulls during that time is the Peak/Surge. To simplify the following examples, we are pretending this generator peaks at 1,200W (it actually peaks at 12,000W).,- A TV that uses 200W (continuous) may temporarily suck up 700W (peak) when powered on. Because 700W is less than 1,200W (peak), the generator will allow the TV to turn on at that level for a few seconds (any longer, and it might cut power as a safety precaution). After a few seconds, the TV then only uses 200W (less than the continuous 300W limit) until the generator is drained,- An unusual device that uses 250W (continuous) and surges to 1,500W when powered on would instantly be shut off by the generator. Why? Even though the device uses just 250W while already on, it jumps to 1,500W when powered on, exceeding the 1,200W pretend surge limit of the generator,In other words, this Enkeeo generator (while using GAS) can power a number of devices that continuously draw up to 9,000W while already running, but cannot exceed 12,000W when one or more devices is initially powered on. When on PROPANE generation, that drops to 8,100W on continuous with 10,800W peak.,SAFETY,- ALWAYS make sure you ground the generator to minimize electrocution risk!,-- Use #8 size wire to connect the generator’s Ground Terminal to a ground source (ie. metal underground water pipe that is at least 8’ into the earth),- Never start/stop engine with electrical devices plugged in and turned on,- Be aware that the starter cord can retract rapidly and pull your hand/arm toward the engine faster than you can let go,- Never add fuel while the engine is hot or running as it could ignite,- Do not overfill the fuel tank so the fuel can expand,-- Overflowing fuel can ignite when spilled against the hot engine,- Do not store fuel in the house (my dad keeps violating this) as they are highly flammable,-- You should not smoke near it. I have seen people do it, and that is extremely dangerous!,- Fuel in the engine’s tank degrades over time. It should be replaced every 6 months even if it was never used,- Never plug the gas generator into a wall outlet to “back feed” electricity into the house to power your appliances,-- This is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS and can electrocute utility workers and neighbors served by the same utility transformer,-- To power appliances in the house, have a licensed electrician install the right equipment for the generator to be plugged in to! THIS IS IMPORTANT!,- Never cover the generator when in use to minimize overheating,- Generator should be used on a level surface,- Don’t use in wet/damp conditions (ie. rain) as you could get electrocuted,CALCULATIONS,The below calculations are rough estimates as conditions, quality, and product age can vary.,How many Watts does a device use?,- Calc: Watts used by device = Voltage x Amperage,- If a vacuum is 120V and 9.5A, it uses 1,140W,How long does it take to charge a device?,- Calc: Hours to charge device = Device’s battery capacity (Wh) / Input Wattage,- If a laptop accepts 60W of input and its battery capacity is 550 Wh, it could take 9.2 hrs to charge (550 Wh / 60W),FINAL THOUGHTS,This Enkeeo gas/propane generator is significantly cheaper than any lithium-ion battery power station I could find for the rated 9,000W running capacity. It provides for a much lower, initial investment for emergency operation, but one should keep in mind the overall maintenance work and cost that comes with gas and/or propane generator use (less so with the latter). With that amount of output, an entire house could be powered with the proper, electrical equipment installed by a licensed technician, and the ability to choose between gas or propane provides for versatility when one fuel source is not available during an emergency situation.,If the company could perhaps expand on the built-in lithium-ion battery with the know-how it already has for its portable battery stations, coupled with solar charging capability, it would make for a killer product.,As it stands, it had been able to run my dad’s multiple freezers and air conditioner with the capacity to power much, much more. Me, on the other hand, will continue sticking to lithium-ion battery stations since I don’t think I would ever need 9,000W of power. That’s a LOT of power.

review_text: My husband really likes his new laser measure.  It has a nice pouch, which he likes because it keeps it from getting scuffed in the toolbox, as well as keeping dust off.  He says the backlit screen is easy to read, which is becoming more an issue for him these days, as it's bright and big.  As he gets frustrated by objects constantly beeping, he likes that he can mute and unmute it easily.  It measures in variations on standard American measurements, as well as metric.  He likes its having two horizontal levels.,He tells me that it's straightforward, and easy to use, though he hasn't yet needed all of its capabilities.  He likes being able to measure from an angle, and that this will tell him what the angle is.  Unlike a tape measure, which you can put out to a length you're looking for, you have to measure against an object, so you would need to walk backward from the starting object.  It measures from both front and back, and can include its own length in a measurement.  He hasn't used the Pythagorean height, but it will be handy to know before we hit the road with the RV again, as there are devices on the roof which weren't there before.  He tells me there are more features which he has yet to explore.,I think this is what I was looking for when I found out after going out to visit my mother in her independent living apartment in a retirement community, that I was going to have to move her to their "memory unit" (how nice of them to tell me what was up before I left home – two days away – so I could pack accordingly).  It would have made it so much easier to figure out what furniture could go where, what was definitely too large, how it could fit in, and just generally plan that move better.  The guys down at Lowe's insisted a tape measure was all I needed, but when trying out variables, this would have been so much easier.,Thank you very much for reading my review. Inexpensive and a great buy!

Review of: **Laser Measure 164 Ft/70M MESTEK Laser Distance Meter M/in/Ft/Ft+in Measure Distance Pythagorean Distance Area Volume - Carry Bag and Battery Included**

I checked the accuracy of this laser measurer and found it to be within 1/16 of an inch every time - definitely good enough for anything you would want to use a laser measure for. This unit is easy to use and the display is quite large and backlit. I also really like the fact that it gives readings in feet plus inches plus fractions of an inch. So you see "5' 8 13/16" " instead of 5.73'. (you can choose metric or other formats of English units too, but I prefer this one). The display shows several previous measurements in addition to the most recent, so if you are doing multiple measurements you don't need to write each one down or remember them. Very handy.

There are also small bubble levels on the unit so you can confirm if the measurement is being done accurately (if the unit is tilted, it can throw the measurement off by a bit depending on how far off level the beam is). And the unit beeps when you take a measurement but this can be turned off if you find it annoying.

And they even included a small cloth case to carry it in, in addition to the strap.

I used this today with my son building an outdoor clubhouse, and it worked extremely well. It doesn't replace a regular tape measure for all purposes, but it is a huge improvement of a tape for many tasks.

After using a few different brands of laser measures, I would highly recommend this Mestek unit - definitely worth the ~$28 price.

I have been a trainer for many years and always felt "shock" collars weren't the humane way to train until our new dog just wouldn't stop barking for no reason. I tried the vibrate and the "shock" mode on myself before I put it on her. 1st, Vibrate mode is a soft shake of the device. My kids and I had fun passing it around to try each level. 2nd, "Shock" mode isn't the type of shock these devices used to have. It's static shock, like dragging your feet across the floor and then touching someone hoping there's a shock for fun. Level 100 isn't fun. Just FYI. And no I did not let my kids try shock mode.  It can work automatically (Auto Anti-Bark Mode) without manual remote control, and it can also be switched to "Remote Control Mode" to train your dog manually. (The receiver collar will enter "Auto Anti-Bark Mode" automatically if you don’t use the remote control in the first 1 minute after turning on the collar. So please press any button on the remote if you want to enter "Remote Control Mode" ),In one day our dog stopped ALL bad behavior. I only used the shock mode once. I start with asking her to stop barking and use the beep mode. She didn't listen so I used the vibrate level 50. She was confused and continued to bark a little. I gave her the enough command to stop and gave her the shock mode level 50. She immediately laid down and stopped. I've never used shock mode since. She is very smart and learned the beep means business. I'd say 90% of the time she listens with the beep and the other 10% is just vibrate on level 25. I ONLY wanted it for problem barking but she is an absolute angel in all ways. She doesn't even beg for food anymore or ambush family when they walk in. She's calmed down and is also more gentle with my kids. She's still the happy, goofy, 90 pound Bernese Mountain Dog she always was but with manners. It's only been 3 days and everyone is very pleased with the results. I love that the seller contacted us twice to make sure all was well. It was easy to set up and use as well. I couldn't be happier to be able to have conversations with folks outside and not have her barking like a psychopath. My dog is the good dog on the block now.

review_text: ,  Your browser does not support HTML5 video.,        ,   This isn't just for babies. We had a tornado a few months ago and ever since my 4 year old stepson has been scared to sleep alone. It's been a nightmare and a lot of sleepless nights. My cousin just had a baby and got this exact model at her baby shower. They sent the link to me and I saw the price and thought no freaking way am I paying that. But we were getting pretty desperate and ended up buying it a few days later. Figured we can just return it if it's not worth the money. Well once we had this up and going my wife was so excited she sent this video to me on the first night. I can't believe how good this night vision is, we can see every detail. The main reason we purchased this though was so we can talk to him when he's scared in his room. He always falls asleep okay but wakes up all through the night scared of tornadoes. It took about a week of adjusting but he's back to sleeping in his own bed alone. This thing ended up having so many more uses that we didn't even think of when buying it. We can watch him now when he's playing in his room and see what he's up to. We've been using a regular old school monitor at night for the past 4 years, just the kind you can hear what's going on. Man have we been missing out. You can move the camera so many angles, we can see almost the whole room, but not quite. It has the option to hang it on the wall, we're thinking about doing that because that would give us complete view of the entire room. It doesn't have to stay plugged in, very portable. Also the battery lasts a very very long time. The brightness variations are fantastic. You can see the temperature of the room for Christ's sake, this thing has everything. The negative aspects are the music isn't that great, but we don't really need that since we don't have a baby. But it does play 5 little lullaby type songs that may be good for a baby. Another negative is this VOX option. We can't even figure out what it means or does. I tried to look it up, but I didn't have much luck figuring out what VOX has to do with this monitor. We thought it meant if it was on we could talk without pushing the talk button but that is not the case. The instructions are very unclear on what VOX means or does. Every once in awhile we get a loud beep in the middle of the night because it randomly loses signal for a millisecond. I don't know why, and I don't mind losing signal but the beep is really annoying. It doesn't happen very often but it does happen. There is a timer on it to save battery, so it can be turned off and turn on when there is movement but we haven't really used that so I'm not too clear how good or bad that works. It's a good option to have though, you can basically make it an old school monitor if you want to but just sound and no picture. Honestly there's so many features on here we haven't even tried them all out. In this day and age I think this is something every parent should own, it's a great piece of mind. My wife really loves it and said I need to tell the world. She's going to be buying one for her best friend's baby shower in a few months. So again I was wrong, it IS worth the price after all

We discovered when sitting on a shelf it doesn't point all the way down, because the shelf was too high. Having it mounted above the crib gives a full view and no worries about it falling over. The whole base of the camera rotates 360 degrees while the head of the camera (lens) rotates back and forth 90 degrees. It even has zoom.,The monitor has a 3 and a half inch screen with a microphone. Maybe it's an age thing. Am I getting old? 😁🤔,I think it's cool that it has night vision and can tell you the temperature of the room. It even plays lullabies, though you can only choose the ones preloaded.,Seriously, all you really have to do is plug it in. It has way more features than I listed or even know about. I had never used a spray gun before, so I was worried that it wouldn't work right, or I wouldn't know what to do but the instructions are easy to follow and that  is a good first step.  A very important thing to do is to make sure you filter your paint before pouring it into the spray container. If you don't filter your paint, you will end up with a clog which will cause the gun to spit and sputter. Also, make sure that your paint is the right consistency. Our paint was was very thick, the container for the gun holds about a quart of paint. In a separate container, I poured in 1/3 cup of water, then about a quart of paint. I stirred, stirred, stirred, until it was mixed super well. Then I poured the thinned mixture through the filter into the gun container. After I was done painting every single time, I took everything apart, and cleaned everything really well. The handle and the motor are one unit, which pulls off of the front part, which is the container and the nozzle. When you're ready to clean the gun, pull off the handle/motor and set that aside. It's the front part that you will be taking apart and washing. There's a little cleaning brush included to help get in the small areas.,I've really had a great experience using this spray gun! I wish I would have gotten it years ago instead of painting with a brush and roller, I could have been using this spray gun! With this gun it will be a breeze!

review_title: It's a very good TRAINING set.
review_text: This kit is extremely light and very good for training or just showing off. The transparent lock allows you to see what is happening inside of the drum and see how the tip you are using is pushing the pins. If anyone is wondering if these tools can be used to open a real lock, the answer is NO.,The tools are too thin and flexible to be used on a real lock: they would bend immediately, or probably snap if you applied more force. The training lock uses very weak springs and one can move the pins very easily., But the amount of force needed to overcome the springs behind the pins of a real lock is such that the tools would irreversibly bend.,Again, these are NOT suitable for real locks. They are very good for training on the provided lock and to show off to friends (or a date) or do magic tricks, but nothing more.

Lately I have been staying home a lot more so I have lots of extra time around the house. I started cleaning up and found a box with lots of old negative films from a long time ago. My friend told me about a film scanner machine that can scan negative films and covert it to digital. How neat is that? I searched around and ended up with this one. This machine was really easy to use. I used the 135 negative adapter with the holder. I just placed the negatives in there and slid it in as I am ready to move to the next photo. This machine uses an SD memory card. If you have the micro sd card that will work too but you will need to put it in the adapter that the memory card comes with. Even through it can hold a maximum of a 128 GB memory card, I think 16GB should be enough (can store about 2000 photos).

To set the best setting for negatives:
1. Power on the film scanner
2. Arrow right to the film type (choose negative and then 135)
3. Arrow over to the resolution and choose 22M

Once you have set the correct settings, you can start scanning the negative films and covert it into digital.
1. choose capture
2. click on convert
3. if you like the picture click ok to save or convert again to cancel.

I got so fast scanning and saving the negative films by just hitting convert and then ok. The picture quality turned out really good. After I was done converting, I wanted to share these memorable pictures with my whole family. I hooked the film scanner to my T.V. via HDMI to get a bigger view of the pictures and it worked fabulously. Old photos are so valuable to me. I am so glad I bought this to help me convert so many negatives to digital. This brings back a lot of memories.

Signal strength and stability - After several hours continuous watching, I can see a noticeable difference between this and my old antenna. Not only do I get more channels, but the signal is stable. review_title: Beautiful, works well, larger capacity=fewer refills, & an amazing value for all of the features!
review_text:
We have been using oil diffusers for years, and go through them quickly because of our hard water (I know you're supposed to use distilled water, but I rarely think to buy it). While not amazing, this has allowed me to try a plethora of diffusers and figure out the features we like and don't like. Features I don't like the most are, even with our hard water - the waterless variety where you drop the oils onto a pad and turn on a fan. These don't shut themselves off, tend to be more noisy, and tend to break down quickly, especially when you forget to turn them off after days of running. Features I do like with the water variety are the auto-off when the water has been expended, those with timers, those you can opt to turn off the light when diffusing overnight, quieter operation and now I know, I lOVE a remote control as well as larger capacity! I wanted to test out a larger capacity one so I could go longer without refills since we tend to use the same scents in the same diffusers, such as citrus scents in our kitchen diffuser, and relaxing scents in our bedrooms.

I read a study where diffusing lavendar for about a week in a row helps our bodies increase natural supplies of melatonin, and while we pretty much only diffuse lavendar and chamomile in our bedrooms, it's rare we do so multiple nights in a row because we just don't think about it, and when we do, the diffuser is often on empty and we're too tired to do anything about it. My 10 year old has been thrown off her sleep schedule during this pandemic and I was trying to find natural ways to help her re-establish good sleeping habits, so put an older diffuser in her room with lavendar, but it didn't have a timer and was pretty small, so we were refilling every night. Also, it was an older model and there was no way to shut the light off. I purchased this particular model because it was one of the least expensive at its size with all of the features we wanted, and I wanted to try out the remote since the outlet we needed to use was across the room on her dresser.

This arrived within a few days and was larger than I expected, though not in an inconvenient way but more so because we've always gotten the smaller standard sizes. We filled it once and my daughter turns it on with the remote in her bedside drawer on nights she forgets to press the button before climbing into bed, and diffuses for 2 hours each night, the first hour of which she reads (not using a device). This is helping her develop a healthier nighttime routine. The first couple of nights, she said it felt forced to put her book down after an hour and try to sleep. Now she can barely keep her eyes open 45 minutes into the book. I'm sure it's not 100% because of the lavendar/chamomile, but the whole nightly ritual is helping. Also, with the larger capacity, she knows to refill it about every 5 days. I'm holding off for a few more weeks of testing this one out to make sure it continues to function correctly, but I will likely get another for our room, and one for my mom who doesn't have a lot of use of her hands after a spinal cord injury, as this will help her operate a diffuser without constantly having to refill it daily, and the remote should be easier to use than pressing buttons on a diffuser when her hand mobility is limited. All in all, I'm quite impressed, and I've already recommended it to a number of folks who love their diffusers, or those who could benefit from using one.

This tool (which is extremely easy to use) just gives me a little peace of mind. The pulse oximeter measures your oxygen saturation level, or the oxygen levels in your blood. It can rapidly detect even small changes in how efficiently oxygen is being carried to the extremities furthest from the heart, including the legs and the arms.,When oxygen saturation is measured using a pulse oximeter, it is referred to as Sp02. If your reading was 82 percent, your true oxygen saturation level may be anywhere from 80 to 84 percent. Pulse oximeters are usually around accurate up or lower than 2%. Thermometers are the same. Typically, more than 89 percent of your blood should be carrying oxygen. This is the oxygen saturation level needed to keep your cells — and your body — healthy. While having an oxygen saturation below this temporarily is not believed to cause damage, repeat or consistent instances of lowered oxygen saturation levels may be damaging.,An oxygen saturation level of 95 percent is considered normal for most healthy individuals. A level of 92 percent indicates potential hypoxemia, or deficiency in oxygen reaching tissues in the body. SpO2 of a healthy person should fall in between 94% and 100%. Supplementary oxygen should be used if SpO2 level falls below 90%, which is unacceptable for a prolonged period of time.,To use the pulse oximeter you add three AAA batteries, stick your finger in over the sensor (picture no 2) and close. It's a very gentle closure and it's SO light. It takes only seconds to read and also turns off after I think 8 seconds. The maximum performance (close to promised maximum) is only possible when the drive is connected to USB C port. Out of the box, the drive is formatted with exFAT which is fine if you’re not planning on using it to store large size files, but if you want to store your large size ISO files (games, software…) you definitely need to format the drive. review_text: This external SSD is awesome. I can honestly say I am impressed as to how user-friendly it really is. It takes a couple minutes to set up and it is ready to use. Windows software takes up more space so it is interesting to see the available space on the PC vs. the Mac when I switched the SSD from one device to the other.,When using it with an Android phone, your Android needs to be compatible with OTG and then not password protected in order to use it for that type of device. So, though we have phones which it would work with, I chose not to turn off password protect. You do get to enter a hint in when creating your password to help you in case you forget it. Otherwise, if you do forget, your data on the drive is lost forever, and the only way to break into it is doing a factory restore. Clearly the data erases... and you get to start again. I do love the password encryption. When it first sees any device it a) has been installed with and b) it registers with, it asks for the password (once you have it set up). The very first time you use it, it prompts the whole password setup process. If plugged into a new device, you must run the installation software and there are folders with the files to guide you.,The amount of storage on this small device is amazing. It is portable and compact enough to fit in a pocket.  The pouch it comes with holds the cables in half, and the SSD in the other half.  It is split down the middle. The device loads up quickly whether on PC or Mac, which is great, too. I wish I had an iPad Pro to try it out with, since they say it is compatible with that device as well.,Cool little storage device with lots of memory... and so easy to cart around. Password protection nowadays is a must. Totally recommend this 1 TB External SSD.

I’m currently using an external Seagate HDD on my Macbook Pro as a time machine and Photos backup.  It takes forever every time when I try to open up my Photo library.  Because of such a large Photo library file, I need to break up my Photos files into smaller ones by categorized them into different years.  The price of SSD has gone down quite a bit these couple years, I finally decided to replace my old external HDD with SSD.,There are so many brands out there such Samsung, SanDisk, Western Digital, Seagate, RAVPower, and many more.  I couldn’t decided which one to get, so I ended up buying both SanDisk and RAVPower; this way I can compare which one is more superior.  SanDisk has tons of reviews and a well-established brand compared to RAVPower, but I heard SanDisk runs hot.  I have a SanDisk external USB flash drive before and had similar issues; however SanDisk is little bit cheaper in price.,I run a benchmark software on both disks - SanDisk & RAVPower on my 2015 Macbook Pro (2.6 Ghz 256GB SSD, A1502) to see which one outperforms.  Again, my computer doesn’t support USB-C; therefore, I’m running on a USB 3.0 and was not able to maximize its speed to the fullest.  To my surprise, SanDisk speed is slower than the RAVPower.  I did a few speed tests and screen shot of the results.,SanDisk speed is not consistent.  I’m getting write and read speed around 351 Mb/s and 305 MB/s, respectively.  Sometimes it goes over 400 MB/s, however it’s not consistent or stable.  On the other hand, RAVPower has been consistently delivered over 400 MB/s write and 422 MB/s read.,Both form factors are pretty compact.  The RAVPower seems to be much more smaller compare to SanDisk.  So if you really care about having smaller size, go with RAVPower, if you want to have your SSD be able to hook on to your keychain, then SanDisk is way to go.  Personally I preferred smaller form factor because I’m always afraid that I might loose the drive if I hook it up onto my keychain.,Finally, SanDisk does get a little warm/hot after a while.  It could be its outer rubbery case that won’t dissipate heat well.  RAVPower is constructed with metal case entirely so I think it dissipates the heat much better than other competitors.  All for all, for little extra money, I'm keeping my RAVPower 1TB SSD for now.  Now that I can open Photos library lighting speed, I don’t need to breakup my larger file.  I’m very happy with my purchase.

The disk is rated for 540MB/s. Actual speed measured with CrystalDiskMark and normal file copy is less than 10% lower but it is still within the expected range because of the age of the computer and test environment not being perfect. I found that the response time was very low. Windows 10 finds the drive really quickly and you can start working with it instantaneously.,The drive can be used with the included encryption software or without encryption just as a normal USB drive. The encryption software works really well though and only adds value to the unit. Installation is easy and fast. The only settings needed is to enable "Safe Mode" and choose a password and optional password hint. The drive is automatically locked when disconnected from the computer. A decryption prompt shows up automatically when you connect the disk. Before the disk is unlocked it will only show up as a 40MB drive containing the software and manuals. This makes it very easy to open an encrypted drive on a new computer. Just connect, install the included software and access the data! When connecting the drive, the data is decrypted and available in a matter of seconds regardless if you have a lot of data on it.,Compared to other drives that I have used in the same price class I have found that the Ravpower SSD performs just as well, and in one case, even better. I found the Ravpower SSD to be superior in usability though. (My only gripe, and it is a small one, with this drive is that the polished black finish on one of the sides is attracting thumb prints.) review_title: SEXY, decently speedy drive for everyday, mainstream computing at a good price
review_text: I have owned, customized, and built a lot of computers over the past 30 years. Hard drives have come a long way in regards to speed and reliability. This market has been dominated by Western Digital, Seagate, Samsung, and have been joined by traditionally-memory vendors, such as SanDisk (now owned by Western Digital). Interestingly, RAVPower has an external SSD drive available. RAVPower has been one of my favorite vendors of batteries and charging accessories at lower prices than the brand names. So, when they suddenly released a SSD drive, I took notice!,WHAT DO THEY MEAN? SATA, SSD, NVMe, M.2, etc...,Hard disk drives (HDD) are mechanical devices whose performance was primarily based on the RPM (revolutions per minute) rating. They were generally 5400 or 7200 RPM (and beyond) -- the higher the number, the faster it would usually perform. As with anything mechanical, they break down over time as the components age.,Flash-memory based Solid State Drives (SSD) were introduced in the 1990s and were VERY expensive. SSD promised resistance to physical shock, faster performance, lower heat output, and more silent operation. Even to this day, SSD still cost more than similarly-sized HDDs.,SSD and HDD connect to your computer via multiple interfaces. Relative to this RAVPower drive, we are only concerned with SATA (internally) and USB-C (externally), a newer USB standard with VERY fast throughput capability.,SATA can connect two drive types:,1. The physically-larger 2.5" SATA SSD (nowadays used in most laptops and desktop PCs),2. SATA M.2 SSD (typically used in Mini PCs and laptops),M.2 SSD can also be connected to the newer, significantly faster PCIe interface: those drives are known as NVMe M.2 SSD.,So, what does all that mean for this RAVPower SSD drive? It's a M.2 and, thus, VERY speedy. Let's look at the PROS and CONS of this RAVPower drive.,PROS,- Very SEXY look,- Good price,- Great performance at up to 540 MB/s. It is not as fast as my Western Digital NVMe SSD (it goes to 2,400 MB/s), but for an external, USB-C drive, it is quite speedy,- Surprisingly SMALL and feels great in the hand,-- Metal casing with a shiny side,- AES-256 encryption through the installation of the included software (it is found on the drive itself),-- Should you lose your drive (or somebody gets a hold of it), they will not be able to read your data without the encryption key/password,- Can be connected as USB-C to USB-C cable or USB-A to USB-C,-- Cables are included for both,- Easy to use,-- Plug it in, and it is ready for use,- Works with Windows, Apple OSX, Samsung Galaxy S9+, iPad pro, and nearly any device that can accept a USB hard drive,- Carry pouch included,- 2 year warranty + 1 year upon registration,CONS,- Not as fast as my existing 256GB WD Black NVMe M.2 drive or Samsung's Evo SSD line,- Performance started dipping around the 15-20GB transfer mark,- LED indicator light (found next to the USB-C port) is small and can be hard to see,-- Light is used to display power on/off and data transfer status,- Sticker ("RAVPOWER" logo side) displaying certifications, model number, etc. makes the device not look sexy. I took it off to reveal a minimalist look to the drive. I wish that the model number (and drive size) were engraved onto the drive somewhere itself. Stickers tend to fade over time,- Shiny piano surfacing on the opposite side of the "RAVPOWER" logo looks nice, but can be prone to scratching. Would have been cool if the LED indicator light lit up behind that glassy surface instead,NOTES,- The drive itself shows up as generic in Windows. It does not appear to be made by one of the main hard drive/SSD manufacturers,- I did not open the case to see what size of M.2 drive is inside,M.2 (behind M.2 NVMe) is one of the highest-performance interfaces you can connect a storage device to. Cost has steadily been coming down, and it is not difficult to recommend this RAVPower drive to the average consumer for its excellent price, great performance, and good looks. I am still very much surprised that RAVPower entered the storage market, but I am glad they have yet another winner under their brand.

review_title: Super fast ssd! From a great company! You won't regret getting one of these!
review_text: So first off this drive is a bit on the expensive side. But totally worth it, it's one of the fastest external drives I've used. Mine totaled 953gb.it has decent locking software included on the drive. But I don’t tend to need these. My testing computer is a 2016 gaming computer, with its aging components this Ravpower drive was still super fast. My internal main drive is a SanDisk ultra 2 240gb SSD (550mbps read and 500mbps Wright). My secondary hdd is a standard 2.5in 1TB Western Digital Scorpio SATA laptop drive. 24gb of 1600mhz ram. I did many copies to and from each drive while some used my system ram to “ boost “ performance a bit. I also cleared this for a fresh copy to see the difference. Some of these actually hit the theoretical limit of my system. A newer system may see slightly higher numbers, or a internal benchmark may also see different numbers, I went for actual file transfers, Make sure to check my screenshots. They show multiple transfers. I noticed many other pictures in reviews showing benchmarks so I stayed with actual transfers. I figured it would be pointless to just show more of the same. This drive is just fast. But remember it's only as fast as your computers slowest part. In my case it's my cpu lanes. I have a few 3.0 ports, but there from a generation ago, I don’t have any 3.1 ports or any type C or thunderbolt ports to test on. But I still commonly hit 200-400mbps, and I believe some of these numbers were because the buffer in my internal drive ran out, but from the ram buffer it hit over 1gbps (see pictures). I also did smaller file transfers. Which also went surprisingly fast, I also compared this to my PNY 128gb 3.0 usb the Ravpower nearly doubled the PNY in each of the file transfers. I’ll post some number with what hdd I went to and from.  I’ll attach pictures of most of these test, some of them go quite fast., Next are technical tests, if your not interested please skip to the bottom.,-------------------------,From Ravpower ssd to internal ssd- 6.45gb single file ( windows 10 install iso file ) took approx 4-6 seconds, approx speed was 1.42gbps (see picuter).,Next was internal ssd to external Ravpower ssd- same 6.45gb file as before, took approx 12 seconds, it started at just over 1.2gbps and at 42% tapered off to 476mbps.,Next was from the internal WesternDigital hdd, to the Ravpower external ssd. It was a combination of the windows 10 file from before and several hundred pictures. This one started at 60mbps then went up to 104 and ran at this speed for the last 13gb. ( 13.5gb total ) took about 2 minutes.,Next was the same file as previous copy, but now it was the Ravpower ssd to the internal Sandisk ssd. It ran at 386 mbps for the entire 13.5gb, took about 30-35 seconds.,Next was the same file again, and went from Ravpower ssd to the Sandisk ssd (second time), this ran 400mbps for 50% of the transfer then dropped to 165mbps for the remainder of the transfer, this took just under 30 seconds.,Next I re-ran the previous 13.5gb file from the SanDisk ssd to Ravpower ssd, it slow for about 4 seconds, it started around 20mbps but quickly ramped up to 240mbps by 10% and ran at this speed for the remainder of the transfer. It took about 35 seconds total.,Next was a folder with approx 24,000 files. 85% were music files most other’s were properties folders and sub folders. It was being transferred from the internal WesternDigial hdd to the Ravpower ssd. It was just under 99gb. It started right at 125mbps, with an estimated 15 minute transfer time. For this transfer windows showed the hdd was running at 82% for the entire transfer. It ran at 125mbps until 82% then the average dropped to 90mbps for the remaining 14gb. The total transfer time was around what it estimated.,Next was the same file of music from the WesternDigital hdd back to the Ravpower ssd. It started at 120mbps, but within 1% held at 30mbps for the rest of the transfer. Which took around a half an hour. Now I believe this was a bottleneck of the internal hdd, as it was at 100% usage the entire time. This was a standard laptop hard drive, most people with entry level computers should expect simular results as this. **Now that being said, moving 99gb in about 30-40 minutes is still amazingly fast. My 3.0 pny 128gb flash drive took nearly 3 times longer for this same transfer. **,Next was a copy of approx 5,000 songs. I had to keep it under 25gb to avoid filling the Sandisk ssd, so I copied 19gb of music. I started by copying 19gb from the Ravpower ssd to the internal Sandisk ssd. It ran at 238mbps for about 10% then averaged 124mbps for the rest, it took about 50 to 90 seconds to copy the 19gb which was around 7,000 files 5,000 of which were music files. The rest were properties files and sub folders.,The last transfer will be from the Sandisk internal ssd to the Ravpower external ssd. It will the the same 19gb as the previous test. This averaged around 170mbps and took about 100 seconds.,I left my system resource monitor running in the background you can see in most pictures so you can see the computer's status while copying., --------------------------,In closing, this hard drive is amazingly fast for its size and price. Has a great storage capacity for its size and was very stable while using. I never had any problems copying or moving files as I have with some others ive tested. It holds a stable speed for most of the transfers so you have a close idea of the finish time. Others ive tested jump around so much you have no clue how long it will actually take. These were all real world tests with actual files, I didn’t use any benchmarks to get my numbers. As shown in the pictures I went solely off of the windows 10 status bar. Most of the time my internal hdd was maxed out while writing or reading to or from the external ssd, which I expected as its rated much faster. Many times it maxed out my internal ssd as well showing its clearly faster then them most of the time. This drive will work for the majority of people even tech savvy people working on computers.

This particular one comes with a razor, eye protection and the actual laser. It also has a manual which is in black and white. I wish that was printed in color because there is a chart for how long you need to use it based on your skin tone but its all grey. I had to guess which shade of grey I was. Since I'm neither white or black I just went with the color in the middle. I used it twice a week for 3 weeks. You have to first shave the hair off and you aim the light at the area you want to remove the hair and then press the button for the light. It takes safety into consideration with the design. There is different leve of strength to use. I went with the first level when I did a test patch. Then I increased to the second level. I didn't feel comfortable increasing it anymore so I did the rest of my treatment with the second level. After a week the hair grew back but it was less than before. I shaved again and did the treatment twice in that week. Every time there is less and less hair. The laser doesn't cause any pain or discomfort and I didn't get any skin irritations from it. My only concern was the manual not being colored. I can probably reach out to the seller and request a colored copy. But if the seller sees this, hopefully they take that into consideration for future production. Everything else about it is great. Its working so far. There is almost no hair growing back on my legs.

We have a 1999 GMC pickup with very few miles on it.  Recently an engine fault warning has been flashing at us each time we drive it.  We have taken it to our local dealer, who read the code as "the number 7 cylinder is misfiring."  They suggested the first thing we try is using a fuel injector additive to clear it out.  They reset the code and we have followed their suggestion, using the truck more frequently to circulate the fuel injector fully into the system and adding more additive to ensure it's had a fair chance to solve the problem.  Unfortunately, the warning light continues to flash.,Since we know what the problem is and the recommended solution for now, I bought this engine fault code reader to be able to reset the warning light ourselves rather than just ignoring it or having to go to the dealer repeatedly.  Since this is a 1999, which we purchased in the early days of 2000, we weren't sure it would work because the product site says it works on "most vehicles from 2000 on,"  however, the fault code reader did a fantastic job.  It read the fault code correctly and very quickly.  It was also easy to use.  There is a port under the dash on the driver's side where my sweetheart plugged it in while the engine was off.  Then he turned the key to on, but not far enough to start the engine.  The reader loaded the information and gave 4 or 5 choices of what information he was looking for.  He chose "engine analysis," which scanned the information from the vehicle computer and allowed him to delete the fault code for now.  While it was still plugged in, he started the engine and the warning light was off.  Then he turned off the engine and unplugged the scanner.  Simple and effective!

Easy to use! this scanner is great for the everyday home mechanic and for the family car owner as well. It’s easy to read, as the code is quickly read and the description displays on the screen- so a separate manual isn’t necessary. This unit can clear codes as well. It is powered using the cars battery, with the ignition on of course, so there is no need to carry batteries or chargers. A great tool to have even if you are not able to clear the code or fix your vehicle yourself- you can at least go the mechanic, already knowing the origin of the code. This will save you time and money, by not being subjected to those extra recommended repairs they frequently pitch to their customers. I was pleasantly surprised with the simplicity and accuracy of this scanner and recommend it to anyone who likes to take a hands on approach to vehicle ownership.

review_title: Full featured, good volume, above average sound quality
review_text: This CIYOYO waterproof bluetooth speaker was very simple to set-up and more than met my expectations.  I purchased this particular model because I liked the physical design.  It is was one of the more elegant waterproof bluetooth speakers out there.  I also wanted a clock display and the ability to use the speaker to occasionally make phone calls.,My only real criticism is that the microphone used for making calls is not very sensitive (or so I am told by listeners at the other end of the phone call).  No one actually complained, but I have heard people say I was fading out when I happened to face away from the speaker, even though I thought I was speaking loudly enough.  This is probably a good thing if you are holding a conversation in noisy environment, like while in the shower.  Though, I never planned to use the speaker to make phone calls while I was washing.  So, the down side is you need to speak directly into the microphone if you want to ensure a good experience on the other end.  Other than the outgoing volume concern, the fidelity seems good on both ends of the conversation.,My recommendation to the manufacturer is that they add a place to attach a cord to the top of the speaker for use in environments where there is no smooth surface to apply the included suction mount, which could be a concern if using this speaker when traveling.,The instructions say that the clock will need to be reset if the speaker runs out of power.  I personally haven't had the battery fall so low that this was an issue for me.  However, I know it is possible to design such devices to maintain their time setting on only a tiny trickle of electricity and it is very common to see clocks holding their time setting even when their batteries seem fully depleted.  So, if this is indeed an issue, the next generation of product should be redesigned to substantially minimize or remove the problem.  Also, the clock on the speaker always defaults to 24hr time when first turned on the time remains accurate, but just switches to military time if the power is cycled.  You won't notice this if you are using the speaker during your morning shower, but it could be an annoyance for those who strongly prefer 12hr time (AM/PM) and plan on using the speaker in the PM.,I will also caution prospective buyers not to assume the photos in the listing are to scale. I have to admit to being quite pleased with the Sabel Inflatable pool.,I have a family of four and so size was a big plus for us with this pool. The one I got is the largest of the available options at 118 x 72.5 x 20in. It's a big enough size to hold three kids or a couple of adults comfortably.,Durability is definitely a selling point for this pool. Made of a durable thick vinyl, it seems to be well made and up to handling the boisterous playing of a bunch of kids. Several repair patches do come in the box in case you get a puncture, but the thick vinyl here is unlikely to get a puncture if you're careful about setup and storage and keeping sharp things away from it. It certainly has held up well to the play days my kids have spent in it several times this spring.,Another review I saw suggested that it came with a tarp to lay underneath it to protect against punctures. Mine did not come with one though I admit that it is not a bad idea to put a tarp underneath it for an extra layer of protection against stones, dry grass and the like.,Setup is fairly easy, but does require an air pump given the size of the air bags. There are three air bags which make up the sides of the pool. Inflation with a good air pump takes about 15 to 20 minutes. Filling with water takes longer, but setup really isn't that daunting with this one.,The instructions do suggest that the pool not be filled past the second ring.  Undoubtedly this is because the air filled rings simply do not have the rigidity to hold back that volume of water (300+ gallons). If it gets overfilled the sides start to bulge.  I do suggest finding as level a surface as possible. Fill level will necessarily be lower if you're on a slope. The water level when filled as instructed is around a foot and a couple inches deep.,On the bottom of the pool are two outlets with drainage pipes to allow for quick drainage of the pool. The six inch drainage pipes are attached to the bottom of the pool drains and lead out to the edge of the pool wall. This is a great idea because it allows the water to drain out without being trapped beneath the pool floor. Natural draining takes roughly an hour. Draining is definitely a big selling point of this pool. It drains at a good rate and saves the user from having to deflate it to drain it.,Overall, I'm really impressed with this pool. I've seen others like it and this one definitely stands out for the better quality materials and the forward thinking in terms of the drain outlets. I really don't see any negatives for this pool aside from needing an air pump to fill it, something I'd have used anyway.
