review_title: Great price for what you get, touch controls are lacking
review_text: I spent a long time researching headphones before I decided to purchase both these Boltune headphones ($50 with coupon) and Soundcore Liberty Air 2 ($100) to compare side by side. If you are wondering why I picked these both, I found that they both had similar features that I was looking for but wanted to see if the cheaper versions were comparable or not.  Overall I decided to that I liked the Boltunes more! They are in a really sweet spot for good price with great features. My only caveat is that the touch controls a really substandard. Here is my full review:,Pros,* 42 hour battery life is insane. Most of the ones I researched were in the 20-30 hours range. Obviously this means the case is larger than most cases but it’s not that big of a deal. It still fits in a pocket or purse,* USB-C type charging port instead of micro USB. It’s nice to have a product with a modern charging port,* IPX8 waterproof which means it can be submerged to at least 1 meter of water. A lot of the headphones I was looking at in this price range were rated at IPX4 or so which means it can’t handle anything worse than a few splashes of water or IPX5 which is a stream of water.,* Bluetooth 5.0 means that there is no lag in audio when watching steaming or online video.,* They sync to your phone as two individual BT headphones so you can use both, or just one. I love this! Some cheaper headphones don’t allow you to listen to one without the other or only allow you to listen to the right ear as a single speaker but not the left which is really strange.,* The connection speed is very fast, by the time you put it to your ears it’s already ready to go. The more expensive Soundcore Liberty Air 2's connection speed was so slow, around 6-7 seconds which is aggravatingly slow.,* These headphones do a great job of allowing you to switch between different sources. Say you are listening to these headphones and then get into your car, the sounds switches seamlessly to the car speakers, and then when you turn your car off it’s easy to switch them back. The more expensive Soundcore Liberty Air 2 headphones I tried were absolutely terrible at switching between devices.,* The sounds quality is great. They sounded just as good as the more expensive Liberty Air 2. I should say I’m no audiophile, but I do use them to listen to music and podcasts.,* The standard ear pieces fit me just fine as a woman, and they come with multiple tips in case you need to adjust.,* The case lid has a satisfying snap to it.  The magnets are strong and keep the lid closed.,* There is one light to indicate charging on the case. The liberty Air 2’s have 3 little dots that tell you how full the battery is (more dots lit = fuller charge). That would be a nice feature to have.,Dislikes – but not a deal breaker,* The headphones lay in the case in kind a weird way that makes it a bit awkward to pick up and put in your ears without twisting your wrist. This is a bit hard to describe, but for example the right earbud is on the right side of the case (earbud facing right, stem toward the middle), when you take your right hand to reach for the bud, you must twist your hand (palm up) all the way to the right to pick them up and then twist your hand palm down to place them in your ear. It actually would have been more ergonomical to have the right earbud on the left side of the case so that you pick it up with your palm facing down and lift to your ear palm still facing down.,Cons,* I’ll be real with you, the touch controls are pretty bad. If you don’t put your finger in the exact right spot nothing happens. Even if you do put it in the right spot sometimes nothing happens. I feel like the success rate of the touch controls is <50% accurate which is not good. The volume controls are also very strange, you have to press and hold for 3 seconds and then the volume will slowly increase or decrease until you let go. Unfortunately since the touch controls are hit or miss you can hold it for 3 seconds and then realize nothing is happening and they have to try again. Sometimes it could take you more than 10 seconds to adjust the volume which is frustrating. I just resigned myself to adjusting the controls on my phone.

review_title: Read all the way! Best thing since sliced bread. Learning curve! Pregnancy sanity saved!
review_text: I read tons of reviews. But didnt want to buy 3 devices. Found a 3 way splitter (mentioned in other reviews). saved my sanity and made us get this auto dispenser.  I'm due with my first in July. I cant free feed my cats because they will get fat (they never used to bother us for food when we free fed them-sigh). They have lost a combined 4 lbs since we started scheduling thier foods & are no longer obese!! But this scheduling came with them bombarding us in the am. Cant have that with the baby coming!,So I took a chance on an open box like new with slight scratches. I'm very pleased to say even the open boxed device works!,I got it a day or 2 before my splitter and adapter, so I used that time to clean and air dry. Install took maybe 12 minutes? Make sure all items/components are tight, secure, & dry!,The programming was prob the most difficult, but its so worth it for the benefits! Now it find it fairly easy! It would be nice if the screen had a blue back light or something so it's easier to see. Think grey screen with black letters; that's what this display is like. When programmed and ready, it shows the buttons are locked and the next time for feeding!,I've heard some say they had issues.,I did buy the adapter separately. I've since had 2 power outages and all I have to do is set the time and then set to custom (vs the preprogrammed cat or dog) and it remembers the feeding schedule without me having to reschedule the feedings! Very thankful for that lil feature since power outages are very common in the summer here!,You will have to force feedings a couple times because the conveyor doesnt have food on it! At first I was like wth! But after doing a couple force feedings, it worked perfectly.,TIP: dont use slow feed unless you have larger portions. Since you can schedule up to 12 feedings with 1/8c as your lowest, I just do multiple 1/4c feedings. The smaller amounts just take way too long to dispense on slow feed!,We use blue buffalo cat kibbles and have no issues with jamming.,It took about 2 months for my cats to correlate the feeder with feeding rather than us making it magically happen. They have now completely stopped tormenting me in the mornings for food!,I give them wet food at night so it's just for morning breakfast and afternoon snack!,I will say we have messes because I cant secure the bowls and the cats drag the bowls, but honestly the cats love the hunt... they go nuts.,Make sure to read the cleaning recommendations! Def dont want to ruin your new life saver!,My cats are brutes! They even tried to bite the lid off. They haven't been able to open it no matter how hard they try. I do see that some say it could be tipped over. Ours is on the floor. They would have to use some serious skill to knock it over with full food for sure. Since I have the splitter, my cats cant stick their paws up for treats.,The only negative I have is that now my cats associate the sound to cereal pouring into a bowl, and they run in all excited and confused lmao

review_title: For home use, filtered water works really well but beware of white dust, everywhere!
review_text: Update_2019-12-19: WARNING---Aquafina bottled water will flood this device's misting port! Each time I've tried to use it OR distilled water in my two humidifiers (including the new model) the misting effect initially appeared to be very good, BUT in short order the misting port began flooding to the point where misting ceased completely until I blotted the excess water from the port. Worse yet, a puddle formed unseen under the bottom of each humidifier. When I switched back to the 16.9 oz bottles of Dasani, that I recently purchased when no 20 oz bottles were available, normal misting resumed. Note that this was with new filters in each, so the blame can't be put there.,Purchased this unit along w/additional filters last winter for the night time use since our much-larger evaporative-type added humidity to only the kitchen & living room area. Additionally, when we had the intense cold from the polar vortex event the larger humidifier drank 4.2 gal every 24 hrs rather than its usual 48 hrs in our apartment with 9'5" ceilings. And despite using an additive we also had to deal with mineral buildup on the latter's two large wick filters. So we weren't about to introduce anything to add to that maintenance burden.,We had a lot of trouble like others mentioned from not following the instructions to the letter. From day #1 we did use one of the recommended water bottles w/the adapter but didn't remove it the next morning since a good bit of water was left. That's mistake #1.,Mistake #2 was connecting the water bottle and humidifier with the unit still attached to the USB cable. Since my hands aren't tiny removing the cord each time is a bit difficult, but since I've been following that practice I haven't dropped either one, and believe me, I dropped it plenty of times before that.,Mistake #3 is allowing water to collect in the misting port. When misting failed to begin I recalled others' complaints and simply dried the port with a tissue whereupon misting started again.,Mistake #4 is trusting that you won't clumsily drop the thin plastic water bottle. After doing exactly that too many times—the last time it landed in the middle of an upholstered piece and emptied half its contents onto it—I then put 3 wide rubber bands where I usually grip the bottle and haven't dropped it once since then.,With that said, even though we're currently in summer weather we still run the Fancii while sleeping due to the drying effect of central a/c. But surprisingly there's been no reduction in its output with the original filter still in place. The only maintenance done 2 or 3 months ago was to apply vinegar on a cotton swab to the misting port with the assumption that there would be some buildup since the filtered water we've been using—rather than bottled or distilled—does not filter out beneficial minerals.,We ran a distilled water machine last winter trying to eliminate the drudgery of dealing w/mineral deposits on our large humidifier's wick-filters from tap water use. Since the same filtered water was used in that appliance there was almost nothing in the way of deposits at the bottom of its tank. That was in drastic contrast to what other users were experiencing from using tap water in their water distiller.,We're so happy with the performance of this small humidifier that we're seriously considering using several smaller ones instead throughout the apartment next winter rather than adding a 13th year of being in thrall to our larger humidifier and its wick filters. We've already purchased a 2nd unit and will purchase a third once the heat is on again.

review_title: I LOVE my Gear S3 Frontier!!!
review_text: UPDATE: 8\12\19,I just wanted to come back and report that my original Gear S3 is still going strong and that I ended up giving it to my Mom who is still using it without any issue. I loved my bluetooth version so much that I purchased another one off of Ebay for a mere $100.00! This was probably 8 or 9 months ago and it is the AT and T version and it was used in like new condition.  I do not use the LTE, I continue to use it as a bluetooth device only and it works flawlessly!! Samsung really hit it out of the park with the  Gear S3 Frontier. I can still get 2 and a half days out of it and it is running the latest software. I can not no comment on the current versions of these watches but if The Gear S3 Frontier is any indication, I'd say get one if you want a smartwatch!,First off, this is my review for my Bluetooth Only model Gear S3 Frontier running Tizen 3.0.0.1 that I purchased here on Amazon from the seller Ocean Reef Electronics.I am using a Nexus 6P running Nougat 7.1.2. Now, on with the review!,UPDATE: Had a defect with the used 6P that I purchased so I returned it and am now using a Motorola X Pure Edition and I must say,  battery life is even BETTER!! I guess it's the better radios in Motorola devices,  so my watch isn't working as hard to maintain a connection maybe?  I'm not sure but it has greatly improved my battery life. It used to be down to about 55% to 58% when I'd go to charge it the next day,  now it's still at at a good solid 78% charge.,*NOTE: Just a suggestion but after having issues with my Fitbit Blaze failing after a year and one month due to the thin layer of film on the back cracking from sweat and causing the battery to overheat and the tracker to die, I decided to put a tempered glass screen protector on the display AND the back panel of my Gear S3 Frontier. Some folks seem to be having the same issue with their S3's that I had with my Blaze and I'm hoping that the additional protective layer will keep my Gear S3 Frontier from suffering the same fate. You may also want to add one as well if you have not already. Just  wanted to throw that in there. Now back to the review!,  I absolutely LOVE LOVE L-O-V-E LOVE this watch!!! First off, I am one of those people who thought smartwatches were just a gimmick to get people to spend money needlessly. The reason I purchased this watch is because I got mad at Fitbit LOL! Seriously. I bought a Fitbit Blaze a year and a month ago and one silly little flimsy piece wore out (because of poor quality material used) and instead of letting me use my offered 50% discount towards a new model tracker that has addressed the admitted material issue, they told me I could either get a free replacement Blaze Pebble (the tracker without the straps)  pay them for a new Blaze or pay them for a model that was inferior to my Blaze. Instead, I went with a free Blaze Pebble, and while I was waiting for it to arrive I came here on Amazon to look at smartwatches. I ended up going with the Gear S3 Frontier and I am SO glad I did!!,PROS:,I live in the boonies and connection is spotty in my house so what can I do now? I can leave my phone in the living room where I get good signal and walk around the rest of my small house and still receive notifications, text messages,  and make and receive phone calls over bluetooth ON MY WATCH!!! I know some folks say the fun of this wears off quickly but because of the poor reception on my phone, it has been an absolute Godsend to be able to leave my phone in a good reception location and still make and receive phone calls and get notifications on my watch. The sound quality is exactly that of my phone on speaker. I use this feature almost exclusively when I'm at home. I don't have bluetooth in my car so I use an output jack in my car and while I don't talk on my watch in the car very often, I do use the controls on my watch to answer calls that go to my phone so I do not have to reach down and get my phone to answer calls. It is so much easier to swipe to answer on my wrist while driving.,MUSIC I  easily figured out how to transfer music from my phone to my watch and I have had no trouble listening to the songs on my watch, both through the built in speaker and by way of bluetooth earbuds without any trouble. I also have no trouble with using the music controls on my watch to control the music player on my phone and I love how quick and easy it is to switch sources right there on the watch screen. Now, I've only tested this in the house. The true test will be when I'm outside mowing grass and I have my phone wrapped in a bandana in my pocket. I imagine it will work just fine but I've not been out to mow since I've gotten my watch. It's so nice, I'm not even sure I'm going to use it while mowing.,UPDATE 10/2/18 I have had many opportunities to use the music controls in and outside the house and they work brilliantly! I am able to use the watch to control the music that I have stored on my watch AND I can also use my watch to control my playlist if I am listening to music that is stored on my phone. Infact you can go back and forth between the two immediately, right there on the watch. I had RF ablations done on the right and left side of my back and both times I went for the procedure, the surgeon and his staff had my play the music on my watch! The first time internet was down and they couldn't access Pandora and I had left my phone out in the waiting room with family so I volunteered to play music out loud that I have stored on my watch. They were all blown away lol! So much so that when I went back a few weeks later for the procedure to be done on the other side of my back, the surgeon said, where's that awesome watch, I want you to use it again to play music! I thought that was funny. :-D,SOS: I have not had a chance to actually try this out but I do have emergency contacts plugged in and I am happy to know I can use my watch to ring for help if my phone is out of reach.,CUSTOMIZATION: I love just how customizable this watch is. Everything is so easy to replace or customize. The bands are easy to replace, the watch faces are easy to change and customize. I use the Gear store as well as the Facer app and while you can pay for your watchfaces, there are so MANY free ones that I can't see myself ever needing to shell out money for new watchfaces. I even purchased some Awinner brand rubber body guards to not only add a layer of protection to my watch, but also allow me to change up the colors of my watch. I like how I can use one of my songs as a ringtone or notification tone and how it give me an option to start the song from the beginning, or where the song becomes enthusiastic, if that is where I would prefer my ringtone to start.,UPDATE 10/2/18 This is an update about the Awinner colored protectors, not the watch watch itself. I mentioned above that I use the Awinner frame covers not only to change the look of my watch, but to protect my watch during periods of high activity but I stopped using them for that purpose because sweat was collecting under the rubber. After 3 or 4 hours of pushmowing the yard, I'd come in and take the frame off and there would be alot of sweat pooled on the inside of the rubber, so much so that I became worried it would cause sweat damage to my watch so now I use the colored frame covers for asthetics only. Right now I'm wearing a gray and black stripped nylon band with the white colored Awinner rubber frame protector and it's kind of looks like I'm wearing Jack Skellington on my wrist! I get a chuckle everytime I get a glimpse of my watch on my wrist, besides it is October right now as I type this lol.,FITNESS FEATURES: Ok let me first start off by saying I am not a super fitnessy person. With that said, I think this watch blows my Fitbit Blaze out of the water with it's fitness capabilities. While I have had a chance to wear both my Blaze and my Gear S3 Frontier at the same time to try and do a comparison, the comparison could not be perfectly accurate because I had my watch on my right wrist and my fitbit on my left. The first time I tested it, of course the watch logged about 600 more steps than my fitbit blaze did, but I think that's because I had the watch on my dominant hand and so far as I can tell, there is no way to adjust that setting like you can on a Fitbit. So what I ended up doing is the next day, I wore the watch on my less dominant hand and the fitbit on my more dominant hand and this time the Fitbit was logging more steps, so I have come to the conclusion, that atleast when it comes to the Blaze and the Gear S3 Frontier, the step count is roughly the same and definitely more accurate if you wear it on your non-dominant hand.,Another fitness feature I love is the "get up and move" nudges! These are AWESOME because they aren't just nudges to get up and take some steps, it actually gives you an option to perform one of three preloaded exercises. "Twist", which is locking your fingers together, pushing your arms straight out in front of you and twisting from left to right. There is "Reach Up" where you do your arms the same but you go up and down instead of side to side. Then there are "squats" where you cross your arms across your chest and push your elbows out and squat down. Or if you don't want to do those options and you'd rather just get up and walk around you can do that too. The only thing I do wish, is that it would keep counting after I do the initial 5 reps. It is neat how it counts them down four you but it only counts 5 and then the screen goes back to the homescreen even if you keep doing the reps. It would be nice to have a bit of continued on screen encouragement from the watch.,UPDATE 10/2/18:,I still love the watch for fitness BUT Fitbit really is on to something with their 250 steps an hour goal reminders per hour because while the move reminders are nice what with having onscreen choices for other activities besides walking, I REALLY wish it were more like the 250 steps an hour that Fitbit has going on their trackers. I wish I could customize and hourly goal or even have the same set hourly goal like Fitbit and get reminders and incouragement that keeps you going for more than  5 counts. I NEED that motivation lol! Unfortunately the fitness aspects of the watch are not quite as motivating as I would like for them to be. I still prefer it for the build quality, over anything Fitbit has to offer though but I really do wish they would update their fitness software to better compete with Fitbit's. I don't even need the SHealth app to be like the Fitbit community, I just want the tracker software to be more like that of Fitbit's tracking software with the hourly nudges and onscreen encouragement.,HEART RATE SENSOR: The heart rate sensor on my watch performs about as accurate as the one on my Blaze did and both where in a few beats of the heart rate sensor I use on the nursing unit where I work.,FIND MY PHONE/GEAR: YEAH!!! It is so nice to finally have a way to find my phone when I've set it down somewhere and I can not remember where lol!,UPDATE 10/2/18 I use the find my phone/ gear feature ALL THE TIME!! I mean, the frustration I have saved (alone) has made this watch worth it to me lol!,BATTERY LIFE: I work at night so I charge my watch before I go to bed during the day so that it can be fully charged by the time I go to bed. This allows me to leave my phone in my living room and still go to bed being able to make and received calls. My battery could probably last me a good two and 1/2 days with the way I have mine set up but I chose to charge it everyday an hour or so before I go to bed. I usually get down to 48 to 53% after a 24 hour period which is quite acceptable to me considering all my watch does. UPDATE: as I stated at the top, I switched to a motorola device and now my battery is at a solid 78% battery life after a 24 hour period the way I have it set up.,CONS:,I only really have one and if they fixed it this watch would be 100% perfect to me and that is the notifications. If you receive a series of notifications from the same source, messaging, facebook messenger, etc, you only see the latest one that was sent to you so if you are asleep or somehow don't notice you've received a message, when you open your notifications on your watch, it will only show you the last response sent to you and none of the previous ones which is probably the silliest think ever. It's not a huge deal for me because I really do not have contact with very many people but if you use your phone for business or you are very social, this is going to bug the heck out of you.,All in all this watch is AMAZING!!!! Easily the best electronical purchase I have ever made and I have absolutely zero regrets so far.

Thankfully I will use mostly wirelessly with my phone or a streaming device to listen to shows at night. The app (Cap Tune) still has a lot of work to go. Tons of restrictions on songs from (not fully downloaded to DRM protection). Other times it won’t even play an available song from the cap time app but will play easily from iTunes.

review_title: Carol Anne, go to the light
review_text: I've had this unit for about a week so far, and it's worked well. I've enclosed a picture of one day's kill of pesky gnats that pop up from nowhere to buzz around my house every summer. It's been like this every day, and I've usually relied on passive sticky traps or simply killing them by hand before.,I've used bug zappers outside, so I knew what to expect. The reviews are right about the sound, though. It doesn't bug me, because each sharp crack means one more dead bug and the end of it's (previously) possible descendants. Each crack, does, however, startle my wife, so that's something you may need to keep in consideration. It's loud but quick, so if you can get used to it, it shouldn't be a problem. After having a gnat buzz around my face, disappear, and a minute later hearing that crack, I experience something akin to sweet vengeance.,Cleaning is easy, as you simply pull the little tray on the bottom out and dump it. For some particularly fried bugs you may need to wipe or rinse, but it's still no big deal. I've done both and have also sometimes just vacuumed them out. Sometimes they get under the tray or outside the unit altogether. This is because not every kill is an instant one. I've seen them zapped and then move around a bit, sometimes walking, sometimes spinning, and then die. So you will find some dead bugs on both sides of the unit if it's sitting on a surface. If it's hanging up, this means dead bugs on the floor, so be prepared for that when you decide where to place it.,The unit is much bigger than I thought it would be. I didn't read the size, but just went by people's pictures, and when it came in, I was surprised. This is as tall and almost as long as my small microwave. It's not too deep, and can be easily picked up in one hand. The power line is short, though, so it will need to put it near an outlet unless you use an extension or surge suppressor.,I don't leave it on except during the day when I'm around, because I don't like leaving anything going while I'm asleep, so this is luring bugs to it that could be hanging around windows trying to get the sun instead. It's still a good idea to minimize any other attractants, though, to maximize the slaughter. I haven't had to do any bulb changing, but I have seen others talk about leaving it unplugged for a couple of hours before touching it. The manual gave like advice, although it may have just been for one hour. Either way, I'd double to it to be safe.,If the unit dies before I feel it's been worth the cost, I'll update this review if I can.

A couple of suggestions for anyone new to these, so you can benefit from my trial and error:,1. Make sure the surface you're applying to is clean, especially kitchen walls which may have unseen residue typical from regular cooking. Otherwise, you may experience issues with adhesion over time.,2. Choose a less humid day to hang these. If that's not an option, wipe your surface area thoroughly with a damp cloth, then run a fan on it for a bit until thoroughly dry. Keep fan running during application if possible.,3. Use more than you think you'll need based on the packaging suggestion. I typically use two pairs of strips (top and bottom) for anything 8 x 10 or larger, or for anything with any weight to it. An extra strip may be more than you need, but trust me, you don't want to end up with less than you need when your cherished portrait comes crashing to the floor. In my many, many uses of these strips, I have fortunately only had this happen once. These strips are quite sturdy.,4. It can be easier to hang items if you first press the strips together, then apply the sticky sides to the item you are hanging, and then finally to the surface on which you're hanging the item. A small level set on top of your picture/item will ensure a nice even look.,4. When removing, pull the tab while applying mild pressure to the strip, holding it against the application surface. This will lessen the likelihood of a chunk of paint from being pulled off.,Overall, this is a great, very useful product which will allow you to hang and change up your favorite decor without damaging your walls. Highly recommended.

review_title: Exceeded My Expectations, Yet Still Pretty Flawed
review_text: This product has a lot of flaws.  It's huge, it's heavy, and takes up a lot of space.  The controls are mind-blowingly, even comically bad.  And they give you a instruction booklet which contains small pages of instructions on how to use it, that doesn't help at all.  You and I couldn't possibly design an interface this bad if we tried.  A lot of people mention how "intense" it is, or that it "hurts".  I'll put it a little more simply: they botched the "difficulty" levels, such that the "easiest" is about as much as most people can take.  Not good.  The makers of this boast about their 1 year warranty.  1 year?  On a $300 item?  Color me unimpressed.  I can't afford to buy a new one of these each year, so I went with the extended warranty.  And how long is each massage anyway?  This has got to be the only such device in it's category that doesn't give at least *some* indication of how much time is left.  Not this device though, you are left looking at cryptic blue and red and green lights blinking at you...having no clue what that means.,Yet, given all those flaws, I'm still giving it 4 stars?  Yep, I am, because at it's core, this thing is absolutely brilliant.  I get a deep tissue massage or two each month, from some pretty amazing therapists, and this machine actually does a surprisingly good impression of a deep tissue massage.  Using this crazy device is actually a fairly enjoyable experience, and I always feel better after going through it.  Great device, I can definitely recommend it, but owch, I can't help feeling each time I use it, how much better it *could* be if they creators put a little more effort and attention to detail when making it.  Hopefully someday there will be a "rev 2" where they fix all the problems.  Until, this is still a pretty awesome device.

review_title: Very quiet hair dryer, albeit a little less in wattage
review_text: This is nice 1600-watt hair dryer. It is pretty lightweight for its size and oddly attractive. More importantly, it is significantly quieter than most hair dryers that I have tried or heard. I really appreciate that I no longer have to hold a high-noise hair dry close to my ears for 5-10 minutes and there is no more high-pitched whining sound to tolerate. However, it is a little low in wattage but good enough for my short hairs. If you have long, thick hair, you may find it a little lacking in power though.,The cord is not retractable but plenty long enough for me (6+ feet long). There are three controls on the handle - two rocker switches for high/low speed and high/low heat respectively, and one push button for a blast of cold air. You need to hold the push button for the cold air to blow though. The rocker switches are easy to select and give you the visual of the particular settings they are in. A detachable concentrator nozzle is provided. A hang loop is integrated into the bottom of the handle, which is handy.,The hair dryer could have use some improvement in ergonomics. I don't find it very comfortable to hold for long duration due to the shape of the handle. It is not terrible but just okay for me. I have had hair dryers that are more much comfortable to hold and grip.,All in all, this is a good hair dryer. It isn't the most powerful but it is very quiet. If you value low noise over power, this is the dryer for you. If you have long, thick hair that doesn't dry as fast, you may be happier with a higher wattage dryer.

It’s Ok. Yes it is quieter compared to the other hair dryers I own but I feel like that has compromised on the power of the dryer too. I have shoulder level hair and this hair dryer takes about 10 min to completely dry it where as my other Revlon, GHD, ones takes just about 4 min ( yup I timed it). The other feature I didn’t like was the cold shot. You have to press and hold this button( that has a snow flake symbol on it) for a shot of cold air. The only problem, the button is very awkwardly positioned so you have to really put all your strength to hold it down and even when you do, it takes a few seconds to switch from hit to cool and if you down press it enough, slowly starts blowing hot air back. It only comes with 1 blow dry attachments. Overall just OK. I wouldn’t recommend it.

This is an easy to read, nice looking weather information center. I have a couple of other indoor outdoor weather units that I know is accurate and they are all in agreement with each other. I would buy this La Crosse weather station again in an instant.

La Crosse has several layouts with similar info so you can pick what you want to look at.  I chose this one for the emphasis on the outside temp.  I can see that from afar.  Time is tiny... don't get this one as a clock.  This one has a couple extras which tipped the scales.  Moon phase is a bonus, pressure graph is a bonus. Remote unit is 10' away with one external wall between.,Now to see if it lasts.,Opportunities for improvement:,- Backlighting has two settings (plus off) that are too far apart in my opinion.  Super bright glowing like the sun, or barely on and worthless unless you're sitting in a pitch dark room.  I'd set it somewhere between if I could but I'll live with the glare of the max setting.,- When you have an atomic clock, accurate to the fraction of a second... it would be nice to have the seconds displayed.  I'll miss that.  But I'll use the smart phone to set the watch in the future... nbd.,- The atm. pressure trend graph... I was hoping it would stop flashing once it got 24hrs of data, but nope.  Dumbest display ever.  7 bars in the graph, it blanks out, then shows you one bar each second... so 7 seconds to wait until you see the trend... then blank again and it starts over.  Hope you got a good look at it in that 1 second where it was complete.  Really lousy design there.  You could do that to the time display or the day text... build the anticipation showing it one letter at a time... but you don't because that would be insane and counter to the goal of displaying info.  This isn't a neon sign in Vegas!  Just show the bar graph and move it when the data fills in.  And if you don't have a number for -24hr, leave it blank!  It'll fill in after a day and in the meanwhile it's accurate and understandable.  Really bad software decision there.,None of that is worth losing a star.,Note on batteries for remote.  Lots of these long time remote things tell you to use alkalines and not rechargeables.  That's because most rechargeables lose power just sitting there so you have to change all the time.  I use Eneloops which do not decay much over time and they worked fine for my last remote unit.  (and any other device with low power needs that need to last... i.e. remote controls),So far, loving the station.  Accuracy looks good so far.

review_text: This review is for Intex Quick-Fill Battery Air Pump, 6 C-Cell Battery, Max Air Flow 420 L/min,The initial challenge is orientating the six C-Cell batteries into the battery compartment.  Unfortunately, the device's battery  compartment has no positive ( + ) or negative ( - ) markings, and the instructions say to reference a picture that is illegible for this purpose.  You can play with the batteries, but there is at least one configuration that results in 1/2 power. The lid holds the only clues, which I figured out after swapping the batteries around for a while.  The quick version is that the end with the hinge and the end with the latch are the only two points where the Negative (-) side goes up.  The remainder of the batteries (despite being right next to each other on opposite sides) are Positive (+) terminals up (see pics).  I am taking away a star for this as they should have marked the battery case with the needed orientation markings OR at a minimum provided clear instructions.  I have provided a pic showing the batteries inserted and instructions next to the pump for reference.  I'd recommend that after you confirm the orientation above woks for you - take a sharpie marker and label each battery spot to save you some time when you need to change out the batteries again.,Once the batteries are properly inserted, it quickly fills my Klymit V Hammock Pad.  The pump offers the ability to move the adapter (if needed) and use the intake port to help quickly deflate your item if desired.  I wouldn't exactly call this pump 'light weight' as it has 6C batteries, but my scale shows that without the batteries inserted, pump with the adapter attached is 10.4 oz / 297.2g.  Since this is a car camping tool, that's an very acceptable weight.

review_title: Light and Stretchy, But Chokes Off Water Pressure
review_text: This is a very nice hose if all you want it for is to water plants with a hand sprinkler attachment.  The hose is very easy to manage - light, compact, etc. - and the brass fittings are top quality.  However, there is an orifice plate in the on-off fitting that chokes off the 5/8" incoming line to what looks like not much more than 1/4 inch.  At first, I thought it was just poor manufacturing, but with some more thought it seems to me that the plate is there to limit pressure on the hose.  The material is so light and expandable that I imagine a full 15+ lbs/sq.in. of faucet pressure might cause it to balloon up and perhaps burst, hence the pressure limiting device.  Like I said up front, that's all fair and well if you want a hose to sprinkle some water on bedding plants, but this hose will not work well with a lawn sprinkler.  I've tried it with two different designs and neither sprinkler throws the water very far.  I even added a water pump onto the end, effectively doubling the line pressure going into the hose, but the orifice plate does its job and there is only a marginal increase in pressure.  I've already ordered a replacement hose made of standard material, but now I'm going to drill out the orifice plate and see what happens.  Stay tuned!

review_text: UPDATE August 2020 - My daughter keeps trying the machine because she knows her high blood pressure (being treated with medications) is still high. DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY!,I purchased this for my daughter because she was getting light headed and suspected that her blood pressure was the culprit.  She had gone to the doctor and received a prescription for blood pressure medication, so my wife and I wanted to get something to her to monitor her pressure (she didn't have anything to do that).  I checked the ratings and found that this meter had very good ratings.  My daughter was very appreciative and had some early success in taking her readings.  But, 3 weeks later, she started to get much higher readings.  Because of the pandemic, she did a telehealth visit with her doctor, who changed her medication after hearing about the high readings from this machine.  Well, after a week on the new medication, she took her pressure and got a reading of 159/111.  Then, she took it tonight and got a reading of 144/92 and then minutes later got 131/85 followed, minutes later, by a reading of 127/81.  Now, do you think that is a meter on which you can stake your health?  Definitely not!  Now, I guess it's possible that she got a bad unit, but we have all lost complete confidence in it. Sad!

review_title: This is it. This is the one you want.
review_text: I was a program coordinator for the American Heart Association and coordinated screening 36,000 people and set up 60 all-volunteer sites. I'm not a doctor so this is not medical advice. I just want to brag about this cuff. In the Heart Association we used to use manual sphygmomanometers (blood pressure cuff) and these automatic ones are brilliant. The problem is some are made better than others. In addition to the manual cuff I have three automated ones. I just sent back the number one seller currently here at Amazon which is $12 cheaper than this one and is probably the reason why it outsells this one, or maybe just because people haven't gone through testing both of these. I bought both of them, this is not a freebie trial.,I sent the other one back because it was inaccurate. It was giving me readings that were 10 points higher than my other cuffs, and I knew it was way off the mark. High blood pressure runs in my family. I'm up in the years. So, getting readings of 108 diastolic (bottom number) on a bad day is a bit unnerving when my other cuffs are giving me 98. Thanks to Dr Fuhrman and his bestselling books, latest being "Eat for Life" my blood pressure has resolved itself, and runs normal a lot of the time. Then I have pizza, or high salt food and bang, I need the pill again. :-),Okay so why is this cuff so great? First and foremost, it is accurate. Secondly the other cuff gave you a verbal readout of the results that was so loud the neighbors across the street could hear it. :-) No way to adjust the volume. This cuff not only can you turn the speaker off, you also have the option to adjust the volume so low someone in the next room wouldn't hear it.,I have a cuff that reads through a cell phone app. You have to boot up your cell phone to use it, and the common error of "measurement failed" happened a lot. Then the Velcro went on it so it would become unraveled in the middle of the test. The cuff has fabulous Velcro that is never going to do that. As a matter of fact, you have to really pull at it to undo it. That's great. It is so strong that a year from now you won't have to replace it.,The video for the setup makes it really clear how to set it up with the date and time etc. for the first use. I also like that it is somewhat compact next to some of the others but not too small rendering it a hobby toy. The size is just right.,By the way the other one, the best seller that doesn't really have a name other than its a cuff is one of those wrist jobs. If you don't have it all the way down close to the very edge of your wrist, you are also getting even higher wrong readings. This one is a full-sized cuff that goes around your upper arm. Just keep the tube area centered on your arm. Doctors and hospitals blood pressure cuffs go around the upper arm, not close to the wrist.,So, this is a serious cuff, that is really accurate, at least the one I have, and I am assuming they are all that way. You will notice that the other cuff has twice as many 1-star reviews due to accuracy concerns. This cuff is down closer to the edge and a single digit for example it is a 3 or 4, next to the 8 on the other one.,So, my advice is getting this one. After setting it up, and using it for the first time I was so impressed and loved the intelligent engineering of it, I gave it a kiss. :-) That is something I reserve for my favorite high-quality guitars when I am done playing them. Hope this helps.

review_title: Bright enough for safety -- you can see in front of you.  But not a security light.
review_text: Disclaimer:  I’ve only had this light for less than 2 weeks.,When I first received the light, I did not install it.  Instead, I first left it facing the direct sun for 2 days to fully charge the internal battery.,Then I left the light in the kitchen on a counter so that every time I passed by the motion sensor kicked in.  Even in the daytime, the motion sensor turned the light on.  So dozens of times each day, the motion sensor was activated.,When it’s dark, the LEDs give off very little light all night long.  If something triggers the motion sensor, the full brightness of the LEDs kick in.,After several days I was satisfied that this product didn’t have an early failure so I installed it in front of my house above the sidewalk.  If the product was defective, I didn’t want to uninstall the lamp and I wanted to test it as much as possible within the 30 day return window.,The sidewalk in front of my house receives almost no light and if something (like a hose or a rake) was left on the sidewalk, someone could possibly trip.  I installed the lamp about 12-15 feet up so that the entire sidewalk was evenly illuminated.,Now when someone comes close to the motion sensor, the full brightness kicks in so that the sidewalk is well illuminated.  The motion sensor is very sensitive and detects a person from (I’m guessing) about 20 feet away.,But make no mistake, this is a good safety light but not neatly bright enough to be considered a security light.  I do have extremely bright hard-wired motion sensor LED lights.,I did buy a more expensive brighter motion-activated solar powered LED lamp for an area that’s always dark that has no electrical outlet.,Naturally, the unit needs to be placed in an area that receives several hours of direct sunlight each day.,I set my unit for Mode 2.  The light is very dim all night long so that the battery isn't drained.  When the motion sensor is triggered, the LEDs are very bright for 15 seconds (I think you can set this for longer).,Summary:  If you’re looking for a low-cost solar powered safety light that’s fairly easy to install, this should satisfy your needs.

review_title: Works extremely well at ridding unwanted insects
review_text: My father in law bought us this exact bug zapper 4 years ago for the old farm house we lived in. He would always joke around that we must have dead things in our walls for the amount of flies we would get in the house every year. We are surrounded by farm fields and the farm house was anything but insect proof. We ran this zapper day and night everyday almost for 4 years until the lights finally needed to be replaced. We built a new house last year and this is our first summer in it. Well, the flies, Asian beetles, and all little flying bugs are still as bad as ever. We are also closer to the fields now and we are seeing more than just flies and Asian beetles. The worst is in the garage and then they come into the house from constant opening of the doors. So, I decided to purchase this unit again because of how much we liked our old one and the bonus was it came with replacement bulbs. So, we used those for our old unit and now we have 2 of these to run. We have one in the garage and one in the house for a couple of days to clean up anything that may be inside. Eventually we will run both in the garage. Just minutes after putting both units up they were zapping bugs. This morning when I went into the garage, there were less amount of flies and it was noticeable. Usually they start flying around when you walk out or you visibly see them sitting on stuff. There were still some around, but not anywhere near what it has been. The house unit also caught a bunch of flies, asian beetles, nats, and even a couple mosquitoes. The unit has an on/off switch so if you wanted to keep it plugged in all the time, but didn't want to use it constantly you can just use the switch. It comes with a chain that you can attach with a clip on the top to hang. I showed a picture of that. The light bulbs are extremely easy to replace. It took just a couple minutes to open our old one and swap them out. The unit is pretty bright, so when all lights are off, it lights up the room. The zapping part is pretty loud, so if that bothers you do not put it somewhere that you will hear it constantly. We could hear it every so often in our rooms when we went to bed, but we do have one inside with us. It didn't bother us, but one of our dogs wasn't crazy about the sound. The tray is easy to dump out. The one downside is the plug isn't very long. So, we made it work in the garage, but both times we have had it in the house, we had to use an extension cord in order to reach an outlet when we have it hanging up. The plug is attached to the top of the unit, maybe if it was attached to the bottom of the unit it would give more length to reach an outlet when hanging up. I wish I would have purchased this a month ago and been able to replace the bulbs in our old one and have 2 running. There would have definitely been less bugs in the house. Oh well, at least we can rid them now. We will use these each season now especially around harvest time because that is when we see a huge increase in insects.

review_title: Great little camera for the price!!!!!
review_text: I read all the bad reviews, though there were many more great reviews. I do understand why the poor ratings were given & I’ve tried to address these concerns below.,My main reason for purchasing this camera is I had major reconstruction on my ankle requiring that my foot be raised above my heart 23 out of 24 hours a day for 6 weeks.  I can get myself to my knee scooter to answer the door, but honestly just want to see if it is someone I want to bother with first.  Thus, the inexpensive camera. If I put a Ring camera on my door, ppl would expect to talk to me. Sometimes I just need to rest or sleep uninterrupted, plus it is a colossal pain in my butt to get myself on that darn scooter.,These are my observations after 24 hours of use:,#1-  I really understand technology. We have a ton of tech toys in our home and my husband & I share the install responsibilities.  The directions sent with the camera are not quite as vague as some of the reviews would have you think. I do understand how to install & setup devices on WiFi, and honestly didn’t even look at the directions after I figured out I needed the QR from the bottom of the camera.  I have an Apple iPhone Xs. The QR code that you need to scan to get the right app for your phone is on the bottom of the camera, not the one in the instruction manual. I downloaded the app, got the camera on my WiFi & had it running in less than 5 minutes.,#2 - The only thing the app needed access to on my iPhone, were notifications pertaining to the TENVISTY app. Someone suggested in their review that the camera asked for access to everything on their phone, this did not happen with my iPhone. I cannot speak to other brands of phones.,# 3 - You also use the QR code to add this camera onto the app using your phone. I did this with my phone. My husband came home after I had already set up camera, so I simply manually input the UID # that I found on my phone in the TENVISTY app settings to add the camera to the app on his phone. The camera does not appear on my WiFi list in settings on our phones.  It may appear on my Mac desktop computer, but I cannot get to it right now.,UPDATE : The camera does show up on my Xfinity list of devices.,#4 - I had to place the camera a good 5 feet away from my glass front doors in order to get a large enough area on my phone screen.,#5 - I found you have to ‘tap’ then move your finger to get camera lens to move. If it does not move in the direction you are going for, it is because you have reached the outer limit of where the camera can move. I suggest you plug it in and play with this feature until you get the hang of it.,#6 - Yes there can be some lag time in movement. I think part of this is when you get to the outer limit of where the camera is able to move. Also, if you have a lot of equipment running on your WiFi, do not have extra pods installed to increase WiFi range, or are running old dated equipment you will encounter lag.,The camera resolution is really amazing. Even my resolution snobby husband was delighted, particularly when I told him how much I paid for it.,I’m on pretty serious pain management, so if some of what I said doesn’t sound quite right I apologize - I just got a bit irritated by some of the negative reviewers.  I will take another look at what I wrote in a few days and correct as needed.,I also have the sensitivity set on low. I have dogs, so when I first ran through the settings I had set it to high and received 37 notifications in the first 8 hours. Again, play with the settings and the rotation of the camera before you get discouraged.  I am ball & chained to my bed right now so I have had unlimited time to experiment.,The camera was packaged very nicely, a la Apple type packaging. There is a mount included you can use for wall or ceiling.,Yes, this is plastic & light as a feather.  You will need to purchase a micro SD card if you wish to record.,For the price and what I was going for, this is perfect.  Enjoy!

My seven year old daughter has insisted for some time that she would like to be a scientist when she grows up. In order to foster that interest, my wife bought her a cheap Meade microscope. It was barely usable, so I went looking for a more serious option that we can use as her interests grow and develop.  This microscope by Swift was just what I was looking for.,One thing to note here is that this is not a new product from Swift. The Swift SW150 compound Microscope is available for purchase and has been for some time. Out of the box you get the microscope itself, two lenses (10x and 25x), batteries to run the lamps, a power cord to run the lamps, a 0.3 MP eyepiece camera, a dust cover, a minidisc with software for mac or PC and a basic instruction manual.  It’s the camera that sets this bundle apart from the regular Sw150 and accounts for the higher price.,One thing to note is that it does NOT come with a phone camera mount as shown in the promotional photos on this product page. The included eyepiece camera makes up for that somewhat, although at 0.3 megapixels, the resolution is only 640x480.  That may seem low, but given that 3MP microscope cameras retail for around 70 dollars (at time of posting), this combo is a pretty good value. The camera does a decent enough job for recreational viewing and it definitely makes for easier viewing for kids. If you need better resolution, a phone camera mount is available separately.,The included software works well enough, allowing for live viewing of whatever is on the stage. Tools in the program allow for changing the color of the image, taking photos, cropping and zooming in among other more complex options for more serious use. I found the software quite usable overall, and my kids, when we put the microscope through its paces, thought it was really neat.,What about the microscope itself? Upon opening the box, I was instantly struck by the build quality.  The microscope frame is entirely metal and it has a nice weight to it. The base is plastic, but the overall weight makes for a piece of equipment that should mostly stay put as you use it.  The fit and finish is really very good as well. It feels solid and the various movable parts are tight and solid. There were no obvious cosmetic issues or build quality issues that I could see.,The microscope itself has many of the expected features, a monocular rotating head, fine and macro adjustment knobs for the stage, top and bottom lights for viewing slides and non-slide items, a diaphragm dial, and three objective lenses. The lamps are switchable with a switch in the back and there is a dial to adjust the lamp intensity for both. The provided power cord allows you to plug it in and there is a battery compartment that uses 3 AA batteries if you don’t want to be tethered.,Viewing is pretty solid. Images are clear and precise without blurriness around the sides. Both lenses work great, though 1000x magnification isn’t very useful in an optical microscope, so while it’s advertised, you’ll probably not go much above 400x.,Bottom line:,For a decent price, you get a robust and solid microscope. It’s well built, works effectively and has a digital cameras for live viewing and photo taking. This is a piece of equipment you can buy and use for years with your kids as they grow through science.

The build quality of this instrument exceeded expectations. It's metal, heavy, and pretty solid feeling, and clearly durable enough to be used in classrooms.,Optically, it's not that great, but most entry level scopes are a little weird optically, especially at higher magnifications. It's good enough to see details you want to see. There are two focusing adjustments, crude and fine. This is very helpful, particularly at higher magnifications.,There are two lights, one below the stage for slides and translucent subjects,. and one above for illuminating opaque subjects. The higher magnifications don't work with the top light because the higher power lens assemblies on the turret put the subject in shadow.  The lights themselves are powered by AAA cells (provided) or a 5v dc USB cable, which is nice.,The instrument comes with two visual eyepieces, one of which has a pointing reticle, which is handy for teaching. It also comes with a camera eyepiece that transmits an image or video to a computer via USB. This is a pretty fun and useful feature, but unfortunately, the image quality of the camera is about as bad as possible: it's 640 x 480 pixels, and is poor quality at that. I'm interested in knowing when this 15 year old technology will be updated, because 640 x 480 is pretty weak. I would upload some of the images I made through the scope, but for some reason Amazon reviews doesn't have a picture upload function right now.,One thing you'll need to make use of this scope is some slides as it doesn't come with any. Pre-prepared slides are useful and fun, and it would be nice to also get some blank slides and adhesive to make your own. If you want to look at creatures in pond water, you'll need a slide with a depression in it to hold the water.,Here's a good set of prepared slides: https://www.amazon.com/AmScope-PS25-Microscope-Biological-Education/dp/B0055DZ3EK/ref=sr_1_6?dchild=1&keywords=microscope+slides&qid=1585938664&sr=8-6,Here are the blank slides with a concavity: https://www.amazon.com/AmScope-BS-C6-Microscope-Depression-Concave/dp/B0186FK6KE/ref=sr_1_6?dchild=1&keywords=microscope+blank+slides&qid=1585938701&s=electronics&sr=1-6,For looking at the critters in standing water, you'll also want an eye dropper to put the specimen on the slide.,Anyway, this is a nice, affordable tool that works and should last a log time.

review_title: This is a great microscope for elementary school to high school students, or for a casual hobbyist.
review_text: I have nothing but praise for this easy to use, solidly build, student microscope. I have a background in light and electron microscopy, and selected this primarily for my 2 elementary school aged children to use. Both they and I are very impressed. I also own a binocular AmScope, and once had an  Olympus BH-2.,The Swift SW-150 is a simplified monocular light microscope,  but it is not a toy. The body is metal and the optics are glass. The under stage led light source has a frosted diffuser and a brightness control. The light can be battery powered or plugged in. The condenser is fixed and there is no diaphragm (there is an aperture wheel that functions in a similar way). It comes with 4x, 10x, and 40x objectives and 10x and 25x eyepieces. At 400x and above the limitations start to show. The objectives are removable. I think the choices Swift made were appropriate for the purposes and limits of this device.  Within its peak functioning range, this microscope produces stunning images. There is not much spherical aberration and no chromatic aberration. You can start viewing slides in under 5 minutes. There is almost no setup and there are no adjustments. My 7 year old has been using it completely independently.,There is an above stage illuminator that I find less useful. It is not very bright and the objectives seems to get in the way. You can get binocular dissecting scopes pretty cheap, but this model has this feature if you want to use it.,The ocular camera is only 0.3 MP, but this is fine. The image ends up being only 640x480, but is useful for multi-person viewing. I was able to quickly get it to work with my Mac (using the Swift software) and with slight effort I got it to work with a Chromebook (using other software).,There is no case (only a vinyl cover). That is really my only criticism.,This is a great microscope for elementary school to high school students, or for a casual hobbyist.,Some images I took with the scope are attached.

I have suffered from back pain for over 10 years and have gone to physical therapy for more times than I can remember, and one remedy that always helped me feel better was the electric PULSE massager (TENS unit) used at the end of each session. I know, how does my back pain translate to the neck? Bear with me here.,A TENS unit sends low voltage electric impulses across the skin that arouse the nerves and lowers the pain. The first time I was on the TENS unit, I was not sure how to feel about it. Sending electric shocks near the areas of my pain gave me concern. When the therapist asked me to tell him/her when to stop as he/she was increasing the intensity of the voltage, I did not know what was the appropriate level. Turns out, whatever I was "comfortable with". I tried a lower intensity at first, but over the dozens of sessions, I had increased it to a pretty strong level, surprising some of the therapist assistants. Why the higher strength? I found that by having the stronger shocks, I felt much more relieved once the session ended after 15-30 minutes. There always was a tingling feeling afterwards, but it transitioned into that of relief. With that experience in mind, let's dive into the neck "massager".,PROS,- Very portable,- USB rechargeable (takes 4 hours from empty to full),- Heating functionality (107F),- 15 levels of electric intensity (at a safe 5v),- Professional looking,- Automatic "massage" mode,- Can be used on the arms and legs. (It probably is not safe to use the electric part on the front of the neck),- Long battery life,- Automatic, 15-minute shutoff to protect against overheating. If it takes you a while to get to the source of the pain, a short timer can be a little frustrating,CONS,- Can be too tight for some thick necks,- Manual provides all sort of health and safety warnings. Be sure to read them all,- Neck is more sensitive than the lower back, and so the electric pulses can feel much more intense,- Battery inside the massager is not replaceable,TIPS,- Wet your neck a bit with WATER first (with a wet cloth) to help facilitate the transfer of the electric pulses to your skin. Don't use oils as they can impede the transfer,- Don't use the massager while driving as it can cause you to be too relaxed or make your neck make involuntary movements,- If you have a pace maker or have metal in your body, you should ask your doctor first whether this device is suitable for you. review_title: I don’t see the value over other models
review_text: Recently, due to the interest of my seven year old in becoming a scientist, I was lucky enough to procure a Swift SW150 compound optical microscope bundled with a .3 megapixel camera. I was impressed with its build quality and value for the dollar and thus gave it a solid 5 star review.,When this microscope, the Swift SW200 popped up on my Vine feed, I decided to get it to see how it compared to the SW150. As such, this review is going to compare the two models. The SW200 is a larger bodied microscope and more expensive depending on the version you get. Both are beginner/intermediate microscopes.,One thing to note before I begin is that there are two versions of the SW200. The SW200 and the SW200DL. At time of writing, the 200DL has been removed from Amazon (and thus I could not look up the price). The difference between the two models is the inclusion of an upper lamp to illuminate the stage. The SW200DL has one, the SW200 does not.,As mentioned earlier, the SW200 is a larger bodied microscope. It has a larger swivel head and a viewing tube that is set at a comfortable 45 degree angle as opposed to the 30 degree on the SW150. It has a slightly larger stage (despite the manual stating it’s the same size as the SW150 at 90mm x 90mm), and degree markings on the fine adjustment knob.  The SW150 has no such markings though it does have the upper stage lamp the SW200 does not.,Build quality on both microscopes is similar with a couple exceptions. The microscope frame is entirely metal and it has a nice weight to it. The base is plastic, but the overall weight makes for a piece of equipment that should mostly stay put as you use it., I did notice that the SW200 has a blue plastic shroud inside the handle. Removing the shroud reveals the channel the wiring for the upper stage lamp would go. The shroud is poorly fitting  on the sides with about 2mm of play for it to slide back and forth, giving it a less than finished feel.,The second issue I had was with the swivel head. Upon using it, I turned it around and noticed it was loose. Out of curiosity, I kept turning it. After five or six revolution, there was a clatter and suddenly I was able to lift the head right off. Inside the gap was a threaded washer that the swivel head screws into. I had a heck of a time getting everything back together.  The only thing I can think is that when it was assembled, it wasn’t tightened properly. I’m not sure if this is a chronic problem with this microscope, but if you get one, be aware that if the head feels loose, you should try to tighten it.,Another thing that jumped out at me was the manual and lack of a warranty card. The SW150 came with an 8 page printed manual with a warranty card. This one came with a 3 page instruction sheet and no warranty card or warranty information at all. It’s silly too because the manual is available on the manufacturer’s website and it’s similar in format to the SW150’s. What, the extra toner and paper was that big an expense?,All that aside, the rest of the microscope experience is really similar to that of the SW150. Like the SW150, it has all the expected features, a monocular rotating head, fine and macro adjustment knobs for the stage, a bottom lamp for viewing slides, a diaphragm dial, and three objective lenses. The provided power cord allows you to plug it in and there is a battery compartment that uses 3 AA batteries if you don’t want to be tethered.,Viewing is pretty solid. Images are clear and precise without blurriness around the sides. I did compare a slide (of a fly’s wing) on both microscopes and could find no real difference between the quality of either, leading me to believe they use the exact same lenses.,Bottom line:,Ok, let’s get to brass tacks. I don’t think this microscope is a good value. It costs just a few dollars less than the (non camera) version of the SW150. The SW150 is a better value. For just a few dollars more, you get the upper stage lamp which gives the microscope a lot more versatility to look at items that aren’t on slides.,My suggestion, get the standard SW150 instead. Same lenses and functionality with the extra lamp for almost the same price. Alternately, buy the SW200DL for a bit more when it comes back on the market. I can’t recommend this microscope over other versions despite it being more than serviceable. The value just isn’t there.

review_text: ,  Your browser does not support HTML5 video.,        ,  ,2nd update( 5 stars to 2):,After receiving the replacement auger I did get this to work again but it sounds like a very loud horror movie soundtrack. There's screeching, high pitch grinding noises and crazy vibrations to the point the plug on the bottom of the strainer jiggles around.,I've done some more research on this model and it appears to be a rebrand of a previous (just as unsuccessful) model which got a lot of bad reviews. I personally thing this is not a good tactic for any company to employ and will not be buying products from them again. The premium price should have come with the expected quality, which in this case is obviously lacking.,1st update:,Well, after using it to extract some celery juice the auger/screw fell apart. The skirt of the screw broke into 4 pieces. It might have been user error since we had it on for a longer time and crushed about 18 full stalks of celery (cut into 2 to 3 inch long pieces) and some kale. It started making a grinding noises after the first 2 minutes of doing this, so we stopped it, rinsed everything out and resumed juicing. It didn't seem to have any places where stuff was accumulating so we presumed the noise was the just some piece of vegetable stuck in a weird spot. Regardless we rinsed it a third time then resumed juicing. After about 10 minutes of use it started spitting parts of unjuiced fruit back in the top basket and that's when we took it apart for the 4th time and saw the screw/auger was broken.,There didn't seem to be anything stuck inside the spinning area that could have caused this so my guess is this one might have been defective from factory. We ordered a replacement screw for 19.99 here on Amazon (from SKG, luckily they sell them) and will report back once it arrives and we give this another try.,Motor is fine, it didn't once stop or slow down, so there was no obvious mechanical blockage that could be responsible for this. Very curious to see what happens next.,ORIGINAL REVIEW:,I was not expecting this to be this good. I've experienced the regular, fast spinning juicers which extract the juice by centrifugal force and are usually very loud.,This thing is quiet, fast (takes about 10 seconds to get the entire juice out of an apple or orange) and surprisingly, easy to clean. They offer a cleaning brush which is very helpful with getting the residue on the bottom of the strainer bowl.,So far we've done carrots, mango, apples, oranges, grapefruit and persimmons and they've all worked out well, no bindings, clogging or any sort of mishap. We even did whole oranges, I would not recommend that, but the juicer ate right through them like a hot knife through butter. At times it will need the push stick, especially with slippery fruits or vegetables ( in our case the mango) but that's easy to do, and kinda fun.,The thing that impressed me most was how efficient at extracting all the liquid this is. Using it with the fine strainer it was expelling almost dry pulp on the exhaust chute. Much better efficiency than a centrifugal juicer.,Overall we love this thing, it might actually keep us on a healthier diet. A definitive thumbs up!

review_title: This gage design is the easiest to use
review_text: I was fully prepared to spend considerable more money on one of the more expensive inflator gages listed on Amazon. However, this particular inflator gage had unique features that I felt were important to its use. 1) The pressure range was 0 to 100 pounds instead of 0 to 250 pounds on the others. I did not have any pressure reading requirements over 60 pounds (Car/Truck tires) and I felt the smaller range of pressure would make this gage more accurate in the 6 to 10 pound range then the gages that had to cover a much wider range. I haven't tested it in the lower ranges yet but it is dead accurate at 30 pounds as verified by my expensive Longacre racing analog gage. 2) I really like the pistol style trigger as when you have it connected to a compressor hose you can get a good grip on the handle of the gage. With the lever style of the other gages the lever gets in the way way when you attempt to grasp the gage. 3) Another great trigger feature is the air pressure input is combined with the air bleed function which is very intuitive to use. i.e. Pull the trigger all the way to put air into the tire then pull the trigger just slightly to bleed the pressure down to the desired level. The chuck works great on the limited tires it was used on. This gage is just sooo easy to use. Now, having saved about $35 over a more expensive gage I decided to purchase a Magna cart (Search for it on amazon) and make a truly portable tire airing system. This system includes A) The Yome gage B) a 10 gallon air tank and C) the Magna cart See attached photos photos. Obviously you still need a compressor to fill the tank. This makes a great system that can go anywhere on my property to inflate tires. Hope this helps your purchase decision.

Basics: The entire footrest is padded, including the sides, and the straps are adjustable. The strap also has a clip so it can be used for different types of trays/seats or hung between two trays if you want to share it. It comes with a bag for storage. The bag for the footrest is 10" x 8". With the footrest inside, it can be flattened down to about 1-1.5" thick so it's easy to fit into a purse or bag. The side pieces are 9" tall, the center is 8.5" long, and it's 7" wide. Plenty of space without being cumbersome. I meant to take pictures on one of the planes and I forgot. I'll have to update my review with those later.,I don't know why I didn't buy one of these sooner. Well, I do know, "it's another thing taking up room in my bag/purse, you have to set it up and put it away. It would be a whole thing. I can deal with discomfort for a few hours..." I'm an idiot. The little amount of room it takes up in my bag and the little amount of time spent hanging it and putting it away is well worth the amount of comfort it provided. This footrest made a huge difference.,I travel often. Anywhere from 6-10 domestic and at least 2 international flights per year. I normally fidget in my seat wishing I had a foot rest. I have back and joint pain due to a degenerative condition and neuropathy in my feet. The thought of being stuck in any airplane seat bums me out to say the least. I had a tightly packed trip overseas with 9 flights in under 2 weeks coming up. I knew I had to order the footrest. Man oh man. Being able to put my feet up meant I could easily reposition my hips and knees making my longer flights so much more enjoyable. I was comfortable! I was even able to sleep! I can't ever sleep on planes. I was concerned that the center panel would bend or crease from use, but it didn't. Time will tell whether that will happen or not, but I used it appx 18 hours and I didn't have any problems with bowing, bending, or creasing. Then again, I'm an adult of average weight and I'm capable of gauging an item's limitations. Be mindful not to put too much weight/pressure on it by using it to push yourself up or anything. If you're overweight and/or suffer from severely swollen extremities, the weight and overall girth of your feet and ankles would factor into how well the footrest holds up, but I can't speak to those variables. I can say that this flat mid section type of footrest would probably be a better option than the hammock style.,I went with the flat mid section version bc it seemed like it would be more spacious, comfortable overall, and shareable. I didn't want a hammock style footrest (one that hangs loosely without the stiff center piece) bc I didn't want my feet to be cramped or pushed together and they don't seem particularly shareable. It worked perfectly for me.,Downside- I could see the plane's crew deciding it was a tripping hazard and asking you to remove it. It depends on the crew and where you're seated, of course. It wouldn't be allowed if you're on one of the planes that has 2 rows as their Exit row since you can't even put bags under the first row of seats. No one said anything about it when I used it on my longer flights. If you're asked not to use it, please don't give the product a bad review for that individual crew's decision. I've seen people do that with other airplane products. If the product is shoddy or doesn't work as advertised, that's one thing, but giving one star reviews based on people and situations that have nothing to do with the actual product is unfair.

review_text: Trimming nails on our three dogs can be a chore. It sometimes takes 2 adults to hold a dog for nail cutting. We charged ours when we got it, used it and then put it away for a month and it was still ready to go when we pulled it out of the drawer.,The first dog I tried the grinder on was our older Boston Terrier. She is extremely mellow and let me grind her claws down without complaint. The guard on the grinder helped me to make sure I didn't grind down too far. There was quite a bit of nail dust that escaped the clear plastic encasement, so you may want to use this outdoors or on a towel indoors. I was very happy with how quickly it trimmed this dog's nails.,The second dog I tried the grinder on was a youngish French Bulldog. She is a more nervous dog and immediately freaked out when she heard the noise of the grinder (it sounds like a dental drill) and fought to escape. I was not able to use the grinder on her.,The third dog I tried the grinder on was a youngish Boston Terrier. He is also a high strung animal and tried to escape the situation when he heard the noise. I was not able to use the grinder on this dog either.,Verdict: his grinder works great if you can get your pet accustomed to it at an early age, or if you have an incredibly laid-back animal. We will keep this nail grinder in with our other pet grooming supplies and use it on the dog who will tolerate it. This is a solid, well-made device and could easily be useful in other non-pet related home repair and multi-purpose DIY projects.
