review_title: Great sound machine for sleeping and relaxation
review_text: I'm pleasantly surprised with this little sound machine. It is great for sleeping and relaxation when a little bit of ambient sound is desirable. It's the size of a alarm clock and lightweight, and quite portable.,The machine has a nice range of natural sounds, fan noise and white noise, such as the sound of waterfalls, ocean waves, rainforest, birds, different types of fans, etc. The quality of the sound is okay. Just don't expect a high fidelity sound. The sound comes from both sides of the machine, so it would work equally well on either side of the bed. One thing though. This machine can get pretty loud. Quite handy if you need it to drown some loud background noise.,On the top of the machine are push button controls - power, volume up and down, fan noise, white noise and natural sounds, loop and timer. The 3 sound buttons cycle through various kinds of sound in their own category. I appreciate that a timer is available for 30, 60 and 90 minutes (3 LED lights to confirm your selection), so I don't have to run the sound throughout the night.,The machine runs on either USB power (5VDC @ 0.5-3A)  or 4 AA batteries. Only a micro-USB cable is provided (along with a user manual). You'll have to provide your own USB power adapter or the batteries. There is a pass-through USB port at the back of the machine, which is handy if you want to charge your phone while the machine is plugged in.,All in all, this is a nice little sound machine for sleeping and relaxation. After trying it out, I have to admit that it works well for its intended purposes. I found it works best at lower volumes, just a bit louder than the ambient noise level. When it gets too loud, it starts to lose sound fidelity and become annoying (especially for certain sounds such as waves and heartbeat).

I was really excited to try this noise machine because I travel quite frequently and never sleep well in hotel rooms because of the noise levels.  While the machine is a tiny bit bulky, it is not impossible to pack in my smaller suitcase.  I like that it has the option to use batteries or an adapter and the USB port on the back is an awesome bonus.  It does not include the wall plug but I just used the one from my phone and then plugged my phone cord directly into the back of the noise machine.,Now on to the sounds…,There are fan sounds, white noises, and natural sounds.  Personally, I only cared for a couple of the fan sounds and a few of the white noises.  The natural sounds were too much and certainly didn’t relax me and encourage sleep.  Totally not a big deal though because I did not think I would love every sound and I really only expected to use the fan noises anyway.  There is a volume up and a volume down which is helpful because it is LOUD when you first turn it on.  It also has a timer for 30, 60, or 120 minutes which I haven’t personally used because I like to keep it on all night.  Overall, I think this is a good noise machine, especially for the price.,*I received this product at no cost in exchange for a fair and honest review.

The player then shows the songs in the same folder structure that shows on the computer, making it very customizable.  I’ve had the mp3 player for over a week now and have only had to charge the battery once, and my son uses it every day!  Overall, I would recommend this to anyone that needs a device that doesn’t connect to the internet that can play music and the radio.  The mp3 player also boasts that it can show pictures and ebooks, but I haven’t tested this feature yet.  I am very happy with this purchase!

review_title: Ingredients, recommended use and effectiveness of the toothpaste
review_text: The flavor of this toothpaste is surprisingly fun, like fruity bubble gum. Kids like it.,That means kids may want more on their brush and to swallow it. Fluoride, so useful for preventing cavities, can also damage teeth or even decrease bone density when too much is ingested. It's important, according to experts, to use the right amount.,The amount experts recommend is only a pea-sized blob for kids 3 and up, or a smear the size of a grain of rice for younger kids, both twice daily. (The pea-sized amount is enough for adults too, though that's less important for us.),Kids should try to spit out the toothpaste, but it's taken into account that most won't be very good at that until they're older. It's recommended that they not rinse, so as to leave some of the fluoride on their teeth to continue to protect them.,Tested,In the interest of science, I've tested this toothpaste on myself for a couple weeks, and compared to a Colgate adult toothpaste. This toothpaste has the same amount of fluoride as the adult kind, as currently recommended.,What I found is that this cleans well but doesn't give quite as much of the smooth feeling after brushing as the adult Colgate. I suspect that's mainly a matter of less abrasives. This toothpaste includes hydrated silica and mica for scrubbing, but maybe in smaller amounts. That may be because baby teeth aren't as hard, but I don't know because Colgate doesn't say.,Ingredients, with comments on safety,Active: Sodium Fluoride .24% (.15% w/v fluoride ion),Inactive: Sorbitol, Water, Hydrated Silica, PEG-12, Cellulose Gum, Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS), Flavor, Sodium Saccharin, Mica, Blue 1, Titanium Dioxide.,Fluoride is a controversial ingredient in some corners, but it's been intensely studied, and it's widely agreed among experts that the benefits, which can't be entirely achieved in other ways, outweigh any risks.,Sorbitol is a naturally occurring sweetener, thickener, and moisture retainer that doesn't promote tooth decay. It can cause digestive upset if consumed in large amounts, but in the amount in toothpaste it's very unlikely to cause any trouble. (Tom's of Maine, famous for its natural products, sees no trouble with it and uses it in some of its toothpastes.),PEG-12 is a polyethylene glycol, another moisture retainer and also a solvent for other ingredients. The manufacturing process can introduce carcinogenic impurities, but they can be removed, which presumably is done here.,SLS makes toothpaste foam up, which helps with spreading it around and carrying away debris. But a few sensitive people find it creates irritation, sores or peeling of mouth tissue. If you notice that, look for a toothpaste without it. (Tom's of Maine offers toothpastes with and without SLS.),Saccharine is an artificial sweetener used because it doesn't promote tooth decay and it's very stable. Early indications that it was a carcinogen were later overturned, and it's now considered safe to eat.,Titanium dioxide is a natural compound used to brighten the color of the toothpaste (not the teeth). In some forms it's suspected as a carcinogen, but toothpaste doesn't use it in those forms. (Tom's of Maine uses it in some of their toothpastes.),One more thing,The toothbrushes are fun and effective too.

review_title: Beware:  Ratings stacked with false reviews
review_text: In concept, I figured paying a little more than the cheapest headphones was going to be necessary to get a decent sound quality and a volume that could be heard over a treadmill at the gym.  In that aspect, the volume and sound, there are no complaints.  Well, except for the fact that you may hear only parts of what you’re listening to, sometimes just through one ear, and sometimes not at all.,The product is inferior and not worth really any price you’d pay for it.  The basic expectation of earphones is that they would reliably function as a device to hear audio through.,To acquaint you with how earbuds like this work, you have to understand that each of the two earbuds work with a touch screen-like interface, except without a screen to view anything on. For example, if you lightly touch one, it will register as a press of a “button”.  This seems sophisticated and high tech, but when you realize that you have to pick them up to put them into your ears, you’ll also realize that you are continuously touching the buttons and giving all kinds of commands.  The problem: the command your message giving it isn’t obvious and the feedback for them is only able to be determined by an audio response... which you can only hear when they’re already in your ears.  By the time you put them in and pressed/turned them into position (by touching them, obviously), you have begun calling a number on your phone, turned one off (you think), unpaired them, and changing the volume while skipping to the previous song. What a nightmare.,The instructions which are written in Engrish can be understood fairly well, so I read them again and again to try and get both earbuds to work at the same time.  Envision this:  your cues for pairing status come via audio through the earbuds and via different behaviors of the small LEDs on each bud.  To see the lights, you have to be holding them (which means you’re pushing more buttons, some of which affect if they pair or not).  If you opt for the trying to troubleshoot a pairing problem by just the audio messages, you can’t see the LEDs that need to be seen to make sure they’re pairing at all.,Finally, I did get the earbuds to pair and heard pretty decent sounding music through them both ... for a few seconds, after which the sound rippled and faded and cut out constantly the whole time I used them.  I thought maybe it was because I was running or maybe it was because there were interfering signals in the gym.  I tried to be understanding and give them the benefit of the doubt.  Later, I tried listening to music standing still in my home while leaning over the phone on the counter and keeping the distance between the earbuds and the phone at about a foot and a half.  Same issue.  Audio cuts out and fades in and out in waves like satellite TV in a horrible storm.  There was never an instance where I heard even 1/4 of a song without dealing with this problem.,The charger box fits the earbuds well, but gives clues to this being a pieced-together product.  For instance, there is a central button inside the charging box.  You can press it and it does nothing.  You can look on the instruction pamphlet that comes with the device, but it’s never even mentioned.,Needless to say, these earbuds are now packed back into a box and ready to make the trip back to Amazon for a full refund and I’ll be shopping for working earbuds... while not trusting Amazon reviews as confidently.

review_title: Good deal on some great headphones
review_text: This is a pretty good set of wireless headphones with a charging case. They are very simple to set up and use. The pairing process is quick and easy with no power switch, they just turn on when you take them out of the case. The headphones are held in their case with magnets, so you just pop them in and they turn themselves off and start charging. The case has a battery and can charge the headphones without being plugged in.,The headphones each have a touch sensitive button on the side. Touching the right ear turns the volume up, and the left ear turns the volume. Double taps act like play/pause and triple taps skip tracks. Its a very intuitive interface and fairly responsive. Sometimes there is a delay, but most of the time the earphones respond as expected.,The sound is good for the price. Don’t expect deep bass tones or crisp highs, but you do get a decent sound, reliable wireless connectivity, and an easy to use interface.

I wasn't sure how difficult it would be to install or how well it would work but I was pleasantly surprised because it took me less than 10 minutes to hook up to TV and another few minutes to scan for channels.  We get more than 40 channels and the picture is great! I'm most excited about saving thousands of dollars a year by dropping cable!

I installed the antenna on my window and the setup was easy (under 5 minutes). The antenna has 3 self-adhesive pads on it to help with mounting. You then take the cable connected to the antenna and connect the other end to the antenna connector to your TV. Finally, plug the power supply cord into the amplifier (it's part of the cable coming from the antenna) and plug the other end into a USB power supply. I'm not sure if it is supposed be part of the kit, but my antenna did not come with a power supply.  Most people probably have at least one of these laying around from an old phone or other USB device.,As far as reception goes, I was able to receive all the analog and digital channels available in my area. I live in an apartment in a rural area, which also happens to sit in a basin. It is probably among the worst set of circumstances for this antenna, so I wasn't surprised when I couldn't receive any channels from a city about 90 miles away.,Overall, it's a great deal on a great antenna, just be realistic about its range for your area..

We live northwest of St Louis by about 25 miles, so the switch for local/distant attracted my attention.  I though I'd have to set it up in a window, and that's what I tried first.  I used the long distant setting first and the TV scanned 44 channels - every local one I expected and a couple others that previous antennas didn't find.  I then tried the short setting and it also picked up the same 44 channels.  The picture was crystal clear and I really couldn't tell the difference in the two settings.  Since it does block part of the view out the window, I then tried a couple of other locations in the room.  I was really happy to find that another scan with the antenna sitting on the floor behind a desk on an outside wall was able to find the same 44 channels with perfect picture quality.  The long cord made it possible to play around with the location much better than those with the standard 6' (2m) cords.  I'm certain I'll buy another one or two of these for other TV's or for my kids.

review_title: Reasonably priced, text alert no subscription security camera with motion detection and night vision
review_text: These cameras are great for our second home which we rent out on short term rentals while not there. The motion detection sends us an alert on our phones so we know when packages are delivered or guests come and go. I recommend putting in the 128 Gig micro SD card which then allows you to go back in time and see what was going on if you didn’t have time to or we’re busy when an alert came through. The cameras also have a microphone so you can also hear what’s going on and we can make sure there are no loud disturbances or parties going on. The motion detectors can be sensitive to our outdoor lights coming on or birds and snow/rain or snow melt but you can easily turn off motion detection and adjust its sensitivity. You can share the alerts and camera feeds with family or caretakers if they download the app and you send them a share link. Haven’t caught any game animals yet but I think it’s only a matter of time. They do require a plug in so you have to plan a little on location and we needed power extensions which were easily available also on Amazon. They occasionally go offline and can be rebooted by unplugging the power and they start right back up but if you live far away and don’t have someone local to do that for you you’ll be offline until you return. Customer support/service was fairly quick and helpful. Overall a great value with lots of features. I really like that I don’t have to pay any monthly subscription. I think they have a cloud service at a modest price if desired. I a very pleased with my purchase and that’s  why I bought a second one and am considering some for my primary residence.

To my surprise, this razor with the #1 attachment left me with a nice amount of stubble and non-irritated skin. The overall quality of this razor is surprising for the price, I can’t imagine much of a difference with products ranging in the hundreds for a simply electric shaver. One of my only qualms with this shaver is the limited area you get to shave while using the non-precision attachments. review_text: This is a small package but is packed with sensors, led lights, and a buzzer. All of this extends the sensors and functionality already available in the micro:bit. Everything on the car can be programmed through the Microsoft Makecode or Python so there are lots of fun educational opportunities. It includes a lot of features found in much more expensive robot kits such as line following, light following (using the micro:bit's built in functionality), RGB led lights, obstacle avoidance, and music. It even extends the large pins on the microbit so you could have components connected by alligator clip even when the micro:bit is plugged into the car. (It's important to note that the kit does not include a micro:bit so you'll need to own one before the robot can be programmed.) The micro:bit is one of my favorite education microcontroller boards and this kit makes it even more fun.

review_text: I've had the G20 for about 3 months and use them daily (primarily for music and media). I've become a fan of ENACFIRE and bought the G20 to upgrade from my ENACFIRE Future Plus earbuds because of sound and feature improvements. The G20 have a low profile and fit snugly, but comfortably, in my ears. The sound is clear, slightly bass-heavy, with great stereo separation. I occasionally use the earbuds for phone calls and they work/sound fine. The ear tips provide good sound isolation (the noise cancellation feature is for phone calls only). The Smart Touch Control features set the G20 apart from competitors at a similar price point. Very light sequences of long and short touches activate/deactivate the earbuds, connect to your phone's smart assistant, raise/lower the volume, pause/forward/reverse your track selection, etc. Other earbuds at this price point (including the Future Plus I previously purchased) have mechanical buttons that are painful to your ear canal because they require quite a bit of pressure to depress. The G20 earbuds pair quickly and have voice feedback to let you know when the earbuds are powering up/down and pairing/connected. The earbuds work as a pair or individually, though some features are only present in one earbud (e.g. the volume up and down functions are split between the right and left earbud). The advertised battery life is accurate and the storage case doubles as a charger.

Just make sure that there is a SOFT SURFACE below the drone because it will fall down from the sky like a rock.,Thank you, Simrex, for another great drone!!!,=================================================================,Original Review is below (this is for older revision and they fixed pretty much everything in the new one).,I wanted to love this drone as much as I have loved Symrex X900, which is great for beginners. But after playing with the drone for over 2 hours so far, I must honestly say that it needs some work. In fact, it took me some time to figure out even how to get the drone off the ground so I almost wanted to give this drone 2 stars. Here is why:,*) THIS IS NOT A BEGINNER DRONE. NOT BY A LONG SHOT.,1) MANUAL. You gotta be joking me. This is NOT a $200 drone manual. NO. The English was surprisingly good and readable/understandable, but the content and usefulness of the manual were just awful. In fact, this manual DOES NOT even bother to clearly outline the starting procedure so I could not get it to fly for an hour or so, which was very frustrating. And do not even get me started about the physical size of the manual and the size of the fonts/pics used in the manual. I have a very good vision, but I could barely see it. Too tiny even though a box could've easily accommodated a larger format manual with properly sized fonts and pis.  To sum it up, the MANUAL is pure garbage. Not good.,2) Initial assembly and calibration of the drone also were quite tricky. There are a lot of things that can be improved or outright need changing. For example, the propellers were not clearly marked so I put them on the wrong motors. The propeller guards are JUST AWFUL. They definitely need to remove that reference from the specs and pictures on this page. Remote is also very inadequate for a drone like this.,4) I still have no idea how to control the camera. In fact, I think mine is broken or something because it just hangs in there and it is not even leveling itself up horizontally when you fly. Maybe the gimbal is broken.,5) SO FAR THE DRONE COULD NOT HOOVER AT ONE POINT and constantly would try to fly away. I can't believe that X900 was solid in this regard at half the price and w/o all that tech like GPS to keep it stable.,6) Something was loose inside the drone (prolly a screw) and the drone overall did not feel very solid in terms of design and materials.,7) SOFTWARE IS GOOD, but no manual and no help so I have no idea how to use advanced functions still.,Basically, I can go on and on, but there are just too many wrong little things with this drone that they really let it down overall when looked at together and in all regards.,I will play with this drone more and post an update but so far I was disappointed and I know for a fact that Symrex can do much better because X900 was awesome and their other toys/drones also quite solid, which is why I like them.,Sorry, Simrex, but you need to do some work on this drone if you want it to be good.,I hope this helps ya all!!!,=========================,HERE IS THE PROPER STARTING PROCEDURE:,1) Turn on the drone.,2) Turn on the remote,3) Move left joystick up, then down and it will beep, it will pair with the remote,4) If you are indoors or have bad GPS signal, press and hold the button on the right upper side of the remote until it beeps (this disables GPS),5) Move, simultaneously, the right joystick to the lower right, and the left one to the lover left, at which point the drone should start.

For my entire adult life (and I'm in my 70's now) every 5 or 6 years I've switched between an electric razor and a manual one. I'll get fed up with one aspect of one and decide to see if I can do better with the other. I decided to try this Braun 5018 about 2 months ago after using a Schick Hydro 5 for the prior 5 years or so. It's my first wet/dry electric and I wanted to see if that would make a big difference.,I first tried it with just water (i.e. wetting my face). Surprisingly close shave but with a little razor burn. Then I remembered that I used to use William's Lectric Shave before shaving with an electric so I tried that. Still nice, close shave but with much less burn. Finally, I tried shaving cream. Very comfortable but hard to see where I needed to shave so I had to constantly feel for where the whiskers were and I missed some as a result. With a manual razor you remove the shaving cream with the razor so you know where you've been but that doesn't happen with the electric.,I'm not sure which method I'll wind up with. But what I can say is that they all yield a very close shave - as good as a manual razor.,Keeping the Braun clean is where there is a major innovation. It has two openings below the shaving head into which you jet water from the bathroom faucet and that rinses out everything from inside. You don't have to take it apart and blow on it and use a brush and all the other stuff that used to be necessary. I've checked it by removing the shaving head and looking inside and it's completely clean. That part is great and a real improvement.,I have 2 complaints which cost the shaver a star. the first is that there is no pop-out trimmer for sideburns. You have to remove the regular shaving head and replace it with a trimmer head. That's a a nuisance. And secondly, Braun doesn't give you any sort of protective cover to shield the foils from damage when the shaver is in the  drawer between shaves.

What comes in the box is the shaver, an extra trimmer attachment, power cord for charging, a mini cleaning brush and the instructions. When I showed it to my husband he was quickly against it having had a bad experience with close shavers in his youth with these particular blades.  However, he was willing to try again, we tested out the trimmer first on his sideburns, back of neck & under the chin to shape his beard. It worked flawlessly, the vibration is powerful & trimmer shaved effortlessly. We then took the plunge and attempted the close shave, popping off the trimmer top was simple, just push it upwards and it pops tight off. Placing the blade on by positioning it on top & it just snaps right in with no fuss. Hubby braced himself while I shaved the leftover soft stubble under his chin bone dry with no cream or water. He could not believe the newfound smooth feeling under his chin. There was no pain as well. His hair is normally soft so he's gone years without needing to do any close shaving as he never has any rough stubble. So this was a new feeling for him and right away he became a fan. We love that it's waterproof as we had just aquired a wall swivel mirror recently which will be perfect for shaving in the shower by angling the mirror towards him. The blades & trimmer are a breeze to clean, simply rinse in water or when it's dry just brush off with mini brush. A 5 minute charge is good enough for one full shave. A full charge will last a few weeks before needing to be recharged. Hubby loves the LED display on the shaver. We also love the simplicity and ease of use this shaver is. The build quality is great, it appears to be well built & solid in construction. There colors are masculine too with a dark base & a splash of light blue. The only con is that at the price point of $80, we were surprised it didn't come with more attachments. Overall we appreciate the build quality & well thought out design that was put into this product to make it easy to use yet functional. We would recommend this item and believe it to be an excellent product. 4 stars.

Update: downgraded to a 2.  Turns out the quality of my voice transmission in conversation with others is significantly worse for them than anticipated.  These headphones have been returned to the seller.,****************************,I don’t know about anybody else, but I have NEVER run into sub-$40 bluetooth headphones with “blow me away” quality.  Because of that, I also never believe the claims of high quality, great sound, yada yada.  These are no exception, but because I know this about myself, I can adjust my expectations accordingly.  Anyway, I really bought these to use primarily for phone conversations while on the move, and listening to music was a secondary concern.  Plus, I didn't want to pay a lot because earbud headphones are notorious for failing eventually regardless of price range.  So I was willing to compromise on some things.,TLDR; I’ve had these now for only about a month and I only use them occasionally (1-3 times per week on the average).  Given my expectations and needs, my overall impression so far is:  On the fence.  Not great, but not bad either, and suitable for my purposes so far.  While I would definitely not put up with this level of quality in a more expensive headset, I am willing to continue with these for the time being.  I give them 4 stars overall for having not-excellent-but-decent-enough quality at THIS price point.,Further details:,No issues pairing with my phone (iPhone 11 Pro).,Comfort:  They're bulky, but lightweight and wearable with the right size earbud tips.,I haven't used them long enough at a time to comment either on battery life or waterproofing other than to say no problems so far.,The power and control buttons are small and close together, making it difficult to distinguish between them by touch.,Noise isolation is minimal.  If you want to walk the city streets while tuning out everything around you (definitely NOT a smart idea anyway, if you ask me), then these are not the ones for you.,Sound quality:  I didn't expect to be blown away by these, as mentioned, but they're decent enough all things considered.  I do NOT hear “deep bass” as claimed by a long shot, nor a sweet top end, but they're not too harsh and they don't sound like they're in a box, so I can live with that at this price point.  A little EQ helps.  And I can hear the person on the other end of the conversation clearly enough, which, like I said, is what I really bought them for.,Which leads me to the mic, which is where things really fall short, and therefore why I’m still on the fence about these.  I don't know what "CVC 6.0 noise cancellation technology" is, but the claim of ”perfect voice transmission in noisy environments" is far from accurate according to the people I speak with.  I live in New York City, so you can bet I know about “noisy environments.”  Things improve while indoors, but the feedback is that my voice still isn't as clear as it is through the handset mic.,Having said all of that, I’m seeing about as many reviews on here praising things like the bass and the noise isolation as there are saying the complete opposite.  As I am definitely not in the camp that’s full of praise for these aspects, I’m left to wonder what those reviewers are used to listening to, assuming my pair are not somehow faulty.  But these things are almost completely subjective at the end of the day, so there you go.  Take it for what it's worth.,Bottom line on these for me is that they’re workable, but the jury is still out.  Will update within a few months if my rating changes.

Over the years, I've learned to trust my instincts (and legit --not bot/fake-- reviews on Amazon) when it comes to audio devices, because with my researched purchases, I really haven't needed to default to big, expensive brand names. However, the noise cancellation of these bluetooth ear buds, and still-stellar battery life, will be worth testing on my next trip.,For the best bass, clarity, and depth of sound, be sure you're using the correct size of ear bud inserts. The "average" size comes already attached to the ear buds, and the smaller size is included in a small bag in the packaging. Also, be sure your phone's music player EQ is optimized for the in-ear experience. The fit is only between two sizes, and not three like a lot of other in-ear products I've used over the years, but the standard size works pretty well for me. It takes some getting used to having ear buds in my ears, and until you do get used to that, you may have pretty sore ears for awhile. I think I'm subconsciously concentrating my ears too much on keeping them from falling out of my ears, much like sunglasses from sliding down your nose, even though they are very secure most of the time. Know what I mean?,I also haven't thoroughly tested the mic quality during phone calls, but I can say I haven't had anyone notice an issue yet. Look to other reviews for more on that, battery life, and bluetooth connectivity distance.,CON: While the outer fabric of the charging/storage case gives it a premium look, I'd rather have a smoother surface so that I can slip it in or out of my pocket easier. Also, the tiny white LED dot indicator isn't very informative or useful for battery level or case-charging percentage/completion. Not really sure what the designers had in mind with that dot, but I wish it had an actual number percentage window, or, at the very least, a single color-changing LED that shows green, yellow, or red for charging completion or battery life left.,Overall, these bluetooth earbuds come highly recommended from a self-proclaimed audio snob :-)

review_title: MONITOR BATTERIES!!!  Very solid gun case and fingerprint recognition works perfectly
review_text: Review of:  **RPNB Gun Safe,Smart Pistol Safe Quick Access with Biometric Fingerprint,Handgun Safe for Nightstand, Security Firearm Safe with LED Breathing Light,11.8"x7.8"x2.2"**,IMPORTANT UPDATE!!! (October, 2020):,I ran into an issue last week with this safe and felt it is important to update this review.  In preparation for a camping trip, I went to remove my handgun from this safe to transfer it into the secured safe in our camping vehicle.  Unfortunately, when I went to open the safe using the fingerprint reader it failed to open.  No beep, no light, nothing.  Fortunately I knew where I had stored the key to open it, and was able to get that from another room and open this up.,It turned out that the batteries had died - again.  I say that because the first set of batteries that I installed back in March had died sometime around June.  I thought maybe that was a fluke, or that maybe I had grabbed a set of batteries that had been used before.  But I know that second set installed only 3-4 months ago were brand new alkaline batteries.  And they died completely on me now, with no alert that they were getting low.  (Note that I don't think I had opened the safe within the last 4-5 weeks.  I suspect if I had tried a few weeks earlier, the batteries would have had enough power left to trigger the indication that they are low, which is a series of 10 beeps and red light flashes),I do NOT open this safe very often, typically weeks at a time between accessing it, sometimes longer.  This should mean the batteries would last longer, but apparently not.  However this also means that if you do not open the safe on a regular basis YOUR BATTERIES MAY DIE WITHOUT YOU BEING AWARE OF IT.,I probably do not need to point out the potential danger of this, in the event you need to open the safe to access your firearm in an emergency situation.  With this in mind, I will be doing 3 things going forward:,1) Switch to lithium batteries, which should have a longer life (I am guessing the electronics on this biometric sensor are consuming a low level of power just monitoring for a key against the sensor, and this is causing it to drain rather rapidly.  Lithiums should help with this.),2) Set a reminder to check the batteries every ~2 weeks.  I suspect this would allow the safe to notify you of low batteries before they completely die.,3) Keep a spare key to the safe hidden somewhere in the same room.  This would allow a relatively fast backup solution for opening the safe in an emergency.  (Must be hidden though or it defeats the purpose of using a safe.),I am reducing my rating from 5 stars to 4, since having to replace batteries every 3-4 months is a bit excessive.  And no where in the instructions or product info does it give a warning that you need to check the batteries fairly often to ensure you do not run into issues.  Nor does it suggest lithium batteries - in fact, it specifically calls out alkaline.,I actually think this thing should probably emit a beep every 5 minutes when the batteries have reached a point where they are getting critically low.  The additional power consumption from the beep would be a worthwhile trade for getting caught off guard by a dead battery.,Last note:  the safe does retain your fingerprints even if the batteries completely die.  So you do not need to program it again after replacing the batteries, even if they have been dead for some time.,Original review (March, 2020):,We were looking for a gun safe that could be used to store a handgun underneath our bed for home protection.  In order to make it easy to access, one primary requirement was a biometric lock.  Historically, these have been very expensive or didn't work very well, but this one looked promising.,So far, we are very pleased.  Programming a fingerprint takes about 10-15 seconds.  You simply place your finger on the sensor while in learning mode three times and your done.  It stores 20 different prints, but thus far, we have only programmed it for two of us.,The best part is the speed and accuracy of recognition.  It literally takes less than a second to detect your print and opens immediately after.  I am actually really surprised at how quickly it detects and opens.  We have been testing this out multiple times a day on a daily basis and I don't think I have had it fail to open a single time.,The safe also comes with a cable that can secure it to something, or it can be bolted to the floor through the bottom of the case.,The metal is very thick and solid and while i am sure a determined thief could bust it open with some tools, preventing that sort of access was not what I was looking for.  Something to keep this out of kids' hands and not leaving a loaded gun somewhere remotely accessible, but allowing me or my wife quick access was the goal.  This delivers extremely well.,If there was anything I would change, it would be an option to not have the safe beep when it unlocks, as I'm not sure I want it making a noise in the event it needs to be opened in silence, like if you did not want to give away your location in a dark house at night.  But I don't consider this a major issue and am not detracting anything from my 5-star review.
